nodes.sql:
-- For each article of the AI Act, the Riksdag AI paragraphs closest to it in a multilingual
-- embedding space, with the Act's passage and the speech paragraph side by side. `similarity` is
-- cosine similarity; `above_chance` marks pairs above the 95th percentile of random
-- speech–Act pairs from the same run (run.json). Semantic similarity only: related language,
-- not influence, response or shared meaning. Derived.
with run as (
    select model, act_version, baseline_random_pairs.p95 as chance_p95 from {{ ref('stg_ai_politics_similarity_run') }}
)

select
    s.article_number,
    s.rank,
    s.similarity,
    s.similarity > run.chance_p95 as above_chance,
    run.chance_p95,
    s.act_passage_id,
    a.text as act_passage_sv,
    s.speech_id,
    s.paragraph,
    p.text as speech_paragraph,
    f.speech_date,
    f.party,
    f.speaker,
    f.debate_title,
    f.source_url as speech_url,
    run.model,
    run.act_version,
    'derived' as content_type
from {{ ref('stg_ai_politics_article_to_speech') }} as s
cross join run
join {{ ref('stg_ai_politics_act_passages') }} as a on a.act_passage_id = s.act_passage_id
join {{ ref('int_ai_speech_paragraphs') }} as p on p.speech_id = s.speech_id and p.paragraph = s.paragraph
join {{ ref('fct_ai_speech') }} as f on f.speech_id = s.speech_id

nodes.name: mart_ai_act_term_diffusion
nodes.subject: cross_domain
nodes.description: Corpus × term list × term × language × month of the AI Act's own terms in Riksdag speeches and job ads, whole months only (derived; never pooled across corpora).

columns.name: corpus
columns.description: Key: riksdag (speeches) or job_ads (ads).

columns.name: term_list
columns.description: Key: primary (the pre-registered terms and matching) or amended (the 2026-10-22 amendment: re-reviewed terms, every token inflected).

columns.name: term_id
columns.description: Key: the term (seeds/cross_domain/ai_act_terms.csv, decision or amended_decision keep).

columns.name: language
columns.description: Key: sv for the Swedish term, en for its reviewed English counterpart.

columns.name: term
columns.description: Attribute: the term as matched.

columns.name: month
columns.description: Key: calendar month, as the date of its first day; only whole months of the corpus.

columns.name: matches
columns.description: Measure, additive within a corpus: documents that contain the term in the month.

columns.name: documents
columns.description: Measure, additive within a corpus: all speeches or ads in the month; 0 in a month without sittings.

columns.name: share
columns.description: matches / documents, null when documents is 0. Fraction from 0 to 1.

columns.name: share_rolling_3m
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: matches over documents summed over this and the two preceding months; fraction 0-1.

columns.name: content_type
columns.description: Attribute: content kind of the row, always 'derived'.

nodes.sql:
{{ config(tags=['ai_act_diffusion']) }}
-- Corpus × term list × term × language × month: documents that use one of the AI Act's own terms, all
-- documents, the share and a three-month rolling share (sums over the window), for the AI Act
-- diffusion clock (docs/ai-act-diffusion-preregistration.md). The terms are the kept rows of
-- seeds/cross_domain/ai_act_terms.csv: term_list primary as pre-registered, amended as its
-- 2026-10-22 amendment re-reviewed them (amended_decision). The two lists are side by side,
-- never merged. Only whole months: a corpus's first and last month count
-- only when its documents reach the month's first or last day. The job ads start in January 2020
-- as pre-registered: the 2020 archive also holds a few ads from late 2019 (117 in three months),
-- whose other ads sit in archives that are not counted. Riksdag speeches and job ads are never
-- added together.
with coverage as (
    select
        corpus,
        greatest(
            case when day(min(first_date)) = 1 then date_trunc('month', min(first_date))
                 else date_trunc('month', min(first_date)) + interval 1 month end,
            case when corpus = 'job_ads' then date '2020-01-01' else date '1900-01-01' end
        ) as first_month,
        case when max(last_date) = last_day(max(last_date)) then date_trunc('month', max(last_date))
             else date_trunc('month', max(last_date)) - interval 1 month end as last_month
    from {{ ref('stg_ai_act_diffusion_sources') }}
    group by corpus
),

months as (
    select corpus, cast(unnest(generate_series(first_month, last_month, interval 1 month)) as date) as month
    from coverage
),

terms as (
    select 'primary' as term_list, term_id, 'sv' as language, term_sv as term
    from {{ ref('ai_act_terms') }} where decision = 'keep'
    union all
    select 'primary', term_id, 'en', term_en from {{ ref('ai_act_terms') }} where decision = 'keep' and en_decision = 'keep'
    union all
    select 'amended', term_id, 'sv', term_sv from {{ ref('ai_act_terms') }} where amended_decision = 'keep'
    union all
    select 'amended', term_id, 'en', term_en
    from {{ ref('ai_act_terms') }} where amended_decision = 'keep' and amended_en_decision = 'keep'
),

grid as (
    select
        m.corpus,
        t.term_list,
        t.term_id,
        t.language,
        t.term,
        m.month,
        coalesce(h.matches, 0) as matches,
        coalesce(d.documents, 0) as documents
    from months as m
    cross join terms as t
    left join {{ ref('stg_ai_act_diffusion_months') }} as d on d.corpus = m.corpus and d.month = m.month
    left join {{ ref('stg_ai_act_diffusion_terms') }} as h
        on h.corpus = m.corpus and h.month = m.month and h.term_list = t.term_list
        and h.term_id = t.term_id and h.language = t.language
)

select
    corpus,
    term_list,
    term_id,
    language,
    term,
    month,
    matches,
    documents,
    matches / nullif(documents, 0) as share,
    sum(matches) over w / nullif(sum(documents) over w, 0) as share_rolling_3m,
    'derived' as content_type
from grid
window w as (partition by corpus, term_list, term_id, language order by month rows between 2 preceding and current row)

nodes.name: mart_ai_act_timeline
nodes.subject: ai_act
nodes.description: Application dates and deadlines from the Act and the dates of the documents that made it.

columns.name: milestone_id
columns.description: Key: id of the milestone, curated (e.g. 'entry-into-force') or 'document-<celex>' for document dates.

columns.name: date
columns.description: Attribute: ISO date of the milestone.

columns.name: source_url
columns.description: Attribute: EUR-Lex URL: the current consolidated text at source_article, or the document itself for document rows.

columns.name: kind
columns.description: Attribute: entry_into_force, application or deadline (curated from the Act), or document (from Cellar).

columns.name: title_en
columns.description: Attribute: short title in English.

columns.name: title_sv
columns.description: Attribute: short title in Swedish.

columns.name: description_en
columns.description: Attribute: English description written for this site; for document rows, the document's title.

columns.name: description_sv
columns.description: Attribute: Swedish description written for this site; for document rows, the document's title untranslated.

columns.name: affected_articles
columns.description: Attribute: semicolon-separated article numbers the milestone concerns; null for document rows.

columns.name: affected_actors
columns.description: Attribute: semicolon-separated actor_ids the milestone concerns; null for document rows or when none are named.

columns.name: source_article
columns.description: Attribute: number of the article the milestone rests on (113, 111 or 6); null for document rows.

columns.name: source_quote
columns.description: Attribute: the sentence of that article, verbatim; null for document rows.

columns.name: origin
columns.description: Attribute: where the row comes from: 'curated from the Act' or 'Cellar'.

columns.name: status_at_build
columns.description: Attribute: 'applies' when date is on or before built_on, else 'upcoming'; the site recomputes it for the reader's date.

columns.name: built_on
columns.description: Attribute: ISO date the warehouse was built, the reference for status_at_build.

nodes.sql:
-- The AI Act's dates in one place: when parts of it apply and the deadlines it sets (curated
-- from Articles 113, 111 and 6, each with its sentence), and the dates of the documents that
-- made it (from Cellar). `status_at_build` is relative to the day the warehouse was built; the
-- site recomputes it against the reader's date.
with curated as (
    select
        milestone_id,
        cast(date as date) as date,
        kind,
        title_en,
        title_sv,
        description_en,
        description_sv,
        affected_articles,
        affected_actors,
        source_article,
        source_quote,
        'https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:'
            || (select celex from {{ ref('int_ai_act_documents') }} where is_current)
            || '#art_' || source_article as source_url,
        'curated from the Act' as origin
    from {{ ref('ai_act_milestones') }}
),

documents as (
    select
        'document-' || lower(replace(replace(celex, '(', ''), ')', '')) as milestone_id,
        published_at as date,
        'document' as kind,
        case document_type
            when 'original_proposal' then 'The Commission proposes the AI Act'
            when 'regulation' then 'Published in the Official Journal'
            when 'amending_regulation' then 'Amending regulation adopted'
            when 'consolidated_version' then 'New consolidated text'
        end as title_en,
        case document_type
            when 'original_proposal' then 'Kommissionen föreslår AI-förordningen'
            when 'regulation' then 'Publicerad i Europeiska unionens officiella tidning'
            when 'amending_regulation' then 'Ändringsförordning antagen'
            when 'consolidated_version' then 'Ny konsoliderad text'
        end as title_sv,
        title as description_en,
        title as description_sv,
        null as affected_articles,
        null as affected_actors,
        null as source_article,
        null as source_quote,
        source_url,
        'Cellar' as origin
    from {{ ref('dim_ai_act_document') }}
    where document_type in ('original_proposal', 'regulation', 'amending_regulation')
       or (document_type = 'consolidated_version' and published_at > (
            select min(published_at) from {{ ref('dim_ai_act_document') }}
            where document_type = 'consolidated_version'))
)

select
    *,
    case when date <= current_date then 'applies' else 'upcoming' end as status_at_build,
    current_date as built_on
from (select * from curated union all select * from documents)

nodes.name: mart_ai_governance_timeline
nodes.subject: cross_domain
nodes.description: Month × series of AI in the Riksdag and in job ads, for one timeline with the AI Act's milestones (derived; temporal overlap only).

columns.name: series_id
columns.description: Key: the series, one of riksdag_ai, riksdag_ai_act, jobs_ai_any, jobs_ai_act, jobs_ai_governance (seeds/cross_domain/ai_governance_series.csv).

columns.name: share
columns.description: numerator / denominator. Fraction from 0 to 1, not per cent.

columns.name: share_rolling_3m
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: sum of numerator over sum of denominator for this and the two preceding rows of the series; fraction 0-1.

columns.name: domain
columns.description: Attribute: source domain of the series, politics or jobs.

columns.name: month
columns.description: Key: calendar month, as the date of its first day.

columns.name: numerator
columns.description: Measure, additive: Riksdag speeches or job ads matching the series in the month; count of speeches or ads. Never add across series.

columns.name: denominator
columns.description: Measure, additive: all Riksdag speeches or all job ads in the month; count of speeches or ads.

columns.name: source_model
columns.description: Attribute: the gold model the counts come from, mart_ai_politics_monthly or mart_job_ai_governance_terms.

columns.name: content_type
columns.description: Attribute: content kind of the row, always 'derived'.

nodes.sql:
-- Month × series: AI in the Riksdag and in job ads, side by side with the AI Act's milestones,
-- for one aligned timeline. Each series keeps its own numerator and denominator and a
-- three-month rolling share (sums over the window); series are never added together or put on
-- one scale. Placing them on one time axis shows temporal overlap only: it does not show that
-- the Act, the debate or the job market caused one another.
with politics as (
    select 'riksdag_ai' as series_id, month::date as month, ai_speeches as numerator, speeches as denominator
    from {{ ref('mart_ai_politics_monthly') }}
    union all
    select 'riksdag_ai_act', month::date, ai_act_speeches, speeches
    from {{ ref('mart_ai_politics_monthly') }}
),

jobs as (
    select
        'jobs_' || term_id as series_id,
        month::date as month,
        mention_count as numerator,
        ads as denominator
    from {{ ref('mart_job_ai_governance_terms') }}
    where field_id = 'ALL' and term_id in ('ai_any', 'ai_act', 'ai_governance')
),

series as (
    select * from politics
    union all
    select * from jobs
)

select
    s.series_id,
    m.domain,
    s.month,
    s.numerator,
    s.denominator,
    s.numerator / nullif(s.denominator, 0) as share,
    sum(s.numerator) over w / nullif(sum(s.denominator) over w, 0) as share_rolling_3m,
    m.source_model,
    'derived' as content_type
from series as s
join {{ ref('ai_governance_series') }} as m using (series_id)
window w as (partition by s.series_id order by s.month rows between 2 preceding and current row)

nodes.name: mart_ai_politics_concepts
nodes.subject: ai_politics
nodes.description: Party (or ALL) × period × concept among AI speeches.

columns.name: party
columns.description: Key: party code, or 'ALL' for every speaker including those without a party.

columns.name: share
columns.description: Speeches naming the concept / AI speeches. Fraction from 0 to 1, not per cent.

columns.name: concept_id
columns.description: Key: framing concept id from seeds/ai_politics/ai_politics_concepts.csv.

columns.name: period
columns.description: Key: a calendar year, a phase (before_proposal, negotiation, after_publication) or 'all'.

columns.name: period_kind
columns.description: Attribute: what period holds: year, phase or all.

columns.name: ai_speeches
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of speeches mentioning AI for the party and period; the denominator of share.

columns.name: speeches_with_concept
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of those AI speeches with the concept in an AI paragraph; 0 when none.

nodes.sql:
-- Concept emphasis among speeches about AI: per period and party (and 'all'), the number of AI
-- speeches and how many contain each concept in an AI paragraph. Periods: the year, and the
-- three phases around the Act (before the Commission's proposal in April 2021, negotiation until
-- publication in July 2024, after). `party` is 'ALL' for every speaker, including those without a
-- party. Shares rest on `ai_speeches`; a small denominator is a small denominator.
with ai as (
    select * from {{ ref('fct_ai_speech') }} where mentions_ai
),

phased as (
    select
        *,
        case
            when speech_date < date '2021-04-21' then 'before_proposal'
            when speech_date < date '2024-07-12' then 'negotiation'
            else 'after_publication'
        end as phase
    from ai
),

periods as (
    select speech_id, party, cast(speech_year as varchar) as period, 'year' as period_kind from phased
    union all select speech_id, party, phase, 'phase' from phased
    union all select speech_id, party, 'all', 'all' from phased
),

with_all as (
    select * from periods
    union all select speech_id, 'ALL', period, period_kind from periods
),

denominators as (
    select coalesce(party, 'NONE') as party, period, period_kind, count(distinct speech_id) as ai_speeches
    from with_all group by all
),

hits as (
    select coalesce(w.party, 'NONE') as party, w.period, w.period_kind, c.concept_id,
           count(distinct w.speech_id) as speeches_with_concept
    from with_all as w
    join {{ ref('int_ai_speech_concepts') }} as c on c.speech_id = w.speech_id
    group by all
)

select
    d.party,
    d.period,
    d.period_kind,
    k.concept_id,
    d.ai_speeches,
    coalesce(h.speeches_with_concept, 0) as speeches_with_concept,
    coalesce(h.speeches_with_concept, 0) / d.ai_speeches as share
from denominators as d
cross join (select concept_id from {{ ref('ai_politics_concepts') }} where kind = 'framing') as k
left join hits as h
    on h.party = d.party and h.period = d.period and h.period_kind = d.period_kind
   and h.concept_id = k.concept_id
where d.party <> 'NONE'

nodes.name: mart_ai_politics_examples
nodes.subject: ai_politics
nodes.description: Example AI paragraphs per concept (newest first) and every paragraph naming the AI Act.

columns.name: party
columns.description: Attribute: the speaker's party code; null for speakers without a party.

columns.name: source_url
columns.description: Attribute: link to the speech on data.riksdagen.se.

columns.name: speech_id
columns.description: Key, references fct_ai_speech.

columns.name: concept_id
columns.description: Key: framing concept id, or 'ai_act' for paragraphs that name the AI Act.

columns.name: paragraph
columns.description: Key: 0-based index of the paragraph within the speech text.

columns.name: text
columns.description: Attribute: the paragraph's text, in Swedish.

columns.name: speech_date
columns.description: Attribute: date of the speech, ISO date.

columns.name: speaker
columns.description: Attribute: the speaker's name and title as in Riksdagen's export.

columns.name: debate_title
columns.description: Attribute: title of the debate item the speech belongs to.

nodes.sql:
-- Example paragraphs for reading the counts against the words: per concept, the six most recent
-- AI paragraphs containing it, and every paragraph that names the AI Act. Newest first; examples,
-- not a representative sample. Each links to the speech on data.riksdagen.se.
with paragraphs as (
    select
        p.speech_id,
        p.paragraph,
        p.text,
        p.names_ai_act,
        p.concepts,
        f.speech_date,
        f.party,
        f.speaker,
        f.debate_title,
        f.source_url
    from {{ ref('int_ai_speech_paragraphs') }} as p
    join {{ ref('fct_ai_speech') }} as f on f.speech_id = p.speech_id
),

by_concept as (
    select
        k.concept_id,
        p.*,
        row_number() over (partition by k.concept_id order by p.speech_date desc, p.speech_id, p.paragraph) as rank
    from paragraphs as p
    join (select concept_id from {{ ref('ai_politics_concepts') }} where kind = 'framing') as k
        on json_extract(p.concepts, '$."' || k.concept_id || '"') is not null
)

select concept_id, speech_id, paragraph, text, speech_date, party, speaker, debate_title, source_url
from by_concept where rank <= 6
union all
select 'ai_act', speech_id, paragraph, text, speech_date, party, speaker, debate_title, source_url
from paragraphs where names_ai_act

nodes.name: mart_ai_politics_framing
nodes.subject: ai_politics
nodes.description: Framing pairs per party and phase, with a balance only from ten speeches.

columns.name: party
columns.description: Key: party code, or 'ALL' for every speaker including those without a party.

columns.name: balance
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: (speeches_a - speeches_b) / (speeches_a + speeches_b), -1 (only B) to 1 (only A); null below ten speeches using either.

columns.name: pair_id
columns.description: Key: framing pair id from seeds/ai_politics/ai_politics_framing_pairs.csv.

columns.name: period
columns.description: Key: a phase (before_proposal, negotiation, after_publication) or 'all'.

columns.name: period_kind
columns.description: Attribute: what period holds: phase or all.

columns.name: speeches_a
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of AI speeches with the pair's concept A in an AI paragraph.

columns.name: speeches_b
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of AI speeches with the pair's concept B in an AI paragraph.

columns.name: speeches_both
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of AI speeches with both concepts.

columns.name: ai_speeches
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of speeches mentioning AI for the party and period.

nodes.sql:
-- Framing pairs (seeds/ai_politics/ai_politics_framing_pairs.csv), per party and phase: how many
-- AI speeches use concept A, concept B, both, and the balance (A − B) / (A + B), from −1 (only B)
-- to 1 (only A). The balance is left empty below ten speeches using either: too few to compare.
-- Descriptive only: which words a party's AI speeches use, not why.
with c as (
    select * from {{ ref('mart_ai_politics_concepts') }}
),

speech_pairs as (
    select
        p.pair_id,
        w.party,
        w.period,
        w.period_kind,
        count(distinct w.speech_id) filter (where a.speech_id is not null) as speeches_a,
        count(distinct w.speech_id) filter (where b.speech_id is not null) as speeches_b,
        count(distinct w.speech_id) filter (where a.speech_id is not null and b.speech_id is not null) as speeches_both
    from {{ ref('ai_politics_framing_pairs') }} as p
    cross join (
        select speech_id, coalesce(party, 'NONE') as party, 'all' as period, 'all' as period_kind
        from {{ ref('fct_ai_speech') }} where mentions_ai
        union all
        select speech_id, 'ALL', 'all', 'all' from {{ ref('fct_ai_speech') }} where mentions_ai
        union all
        select speech_id, coalesce(party, 'NONE'),
            case when speech_date < date '2021-04-21' then 'before_proposal'
                 when speech_date < date '2024-07-12' then 'negotiation' else 'after_publication' end,
            'phase'
        from {{ ref('fct_ai_speech') }} where mentions_ai
        union all
        select speech_id, 'ALL',
            case when speech_date < date '2021-04-21' then 'before_proposal'
                 when speech_date < date '2024-07-12' then 'negotiation' else 'after_publication' end,
            'phase'
        from {{ ref('fct_ai_speech') }} where mentions_ai
    ) as w
    left join {{ ref('int_ai_speech_concepts') }} as a on a.speech_id = w.speech_id and a.concept_id = p.concept_a
    left join {{ ref('int_ai_speech_concepts') }} as b on b.speech_id = w.speech_id and b.concept_id = p.concept_b
    group by all
)

select
    s.*,
    d.ai_speeches,
    case when s.speeches_a + s.speeches_b >= 10
        then (s.speeches_a - s.speeches_b) / (s.speeches_a + s.speeches_b) end as balance
from speech_pairs as s
join (select distinct party, period, ai_speeches from c) as d
    on d.party = s.party and d.period = s.period
where s.party <> 'NONE'

nodes.name: mart_ai_politics_monthly
nodes.subject: ai_politics
nodes.description: Month × all speeches, AI speeches and AI Act speeches, shares and a three-month rolling share.

columns.name: month
columns.description: Key: first day of the calendar month.

columns.name: ai_share
columns.description: AI speeches / all speeches in the month. Fraction from 0 to 1, not per cent.

columns.name: speeches
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of Riksdag speeches in the month.

columns.name: ai_speeches
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of speeches in the month that mention AI.

columns.name: ai_act_speeches
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of speeches in the month that name the AI Act.

columns.name: ai_share_rolling_3m
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: AI speeches / speeches summed over this and the two preceding months; fraction 0-1.

columns.name: speeches_rolling_3m
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: count of speeches in this and the two preceding months (a rolling window, so rows overlap).

nodes.sql:
-- Month by month: all speeches, speeches about AI and speeches naming the AI Act, with shares and
-- a three-month rolling share (sums over the window, not an average of shares).
with monthly as (
    select
        speech_month as month,
        count(*) as speeches,
        count(*) filter (where mentions_ai) as ai_speeches,
        count(*) filter (where names_ai_act) as ai_act_speeches
    from {{ ref('fct_ai_speech') }}
    group by speech_month
)

select
    month,
    speeches,
    ai_speeches,
    ai_act_speeches,
    ai_speeches / speeches as ai_share,
    sum(ai_speeches) over w / sum(speeches) over w as ai_share_rolling_3m,
    sum(speeches) over w as speeches_rolling_3m
from monthly
window w as (order by month rows between 2 preceding and current row)
order by month

nodes.name: mart_ai_politics_party_year
nodes.subject: ai_politics
nodes.description: Party × year, share of speeches mentioning AI.

columns.name: ai_share
columns.description: The party's AI speeches / all its speeches in the year. Fraction from 0 to 1, not per cent.

columns.name: party
columns.description: Key, references dim_party: party code; speakers without a party are left out.

columns.name: year
columns.description: Key: calendar year of the speeches.

columns.name: speeches
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of the party's speeches in the year.

columns.name: ai_speeches
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of the party's speeches in the year that mention AI.

columns.name: ai_act_speeches
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of the party's speeches in the year that name the AI Act.

nodes.sql:
-- Party × calendar year: how many of the party's speeches mention AI, and the share.
select
    party,
    speech_year as year,
    count(*) as speeches,
    count(*) filter (where mentions_ai) as ai_speeches,
    count(*) filter (where mentions_ai) / count(*) as ai_share,
    count(*) filter (where names_ai_act) as ai_act_speeches
from {{ ref('fct_ai_speech') }}
where party is not null
group by party, speech_year

nodes.sql:
-- One row per analytical validity diagnostic: question, target construct, proxy measure, the
-- diagnostic's result (derived, read from the pipelines' own artefacts), its status
-- (supported, warning, insufficient_evidence, invalidated, not_evaluated) and a person's
-- interpretation. Kept apart from data quality: correct data can support an invalid conclusion.
select
    analysis_id,
    product_id,
    kind,
    analysis_order,
    diagnostic_order,
    question_en,
    question_sv,
    target_construct,
    proxy_measure,
    diagnostic_id,
    diagnostic,
    experiment,
    result,
    details,
    rule,
    status,
    analysis_status,
    interpretation,
    conclusion_en,
    conclusion_sv,
    source,
    evaluated_at::timestamptz as evaluated_at,
    'derived' as result_content_type,
    'interpretation' as interpretation_content_type
from {{ ref('stg_quality_validity') }}

nodes.name: mart_budget_context

nodes.name: mart_budget_language_gap
nodes.subject: politics
nodes.description: Exact-key join of the corrected party frame and the language audit, only for party proposals that cover all 27 expenditure areas. Delivered as gold/tables/mart_budget_language_gap.json, where attention_minus_budget_pp is formed. Descriptive difference; speeches may come after the budget proposal.

columns.name: corpus
columns.description: Key: speech archive the audit read, leaders (party-leader debates) or issues (issue debates).

columns.name: method
columns.description: Key: keyword matching method, exact (token equals a keyword) or stem (Swedish Snowball stem equals a keyword's stem).

columns.name: session
columns.description: Key, references dim_parliament_session: riksmöte, e.g. 2024/25.

columns.name: party
columns.description: Key, references dim_party: party code (C, KD, L, M, MP, S, SD, V).

columns.name: expenditure_area
columns.description: Key: expenditure area (utgiftsområde) number, 1-27.

columns.name: budget_year_start
columns.description: Attribute: first day of budget_year, ISO date; the time dimension.

columns.name: budget_year
columns.description: Attribute: calendar year the party's budget proposal applies to.

columns.name: amount_msek
columns.description: Measure, additive: party's proposed frame for the area; million SEK.

columns.name: budget_share_pct
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: area's share of the party's whole frame, per cent 0-100; adds to 100 over areas.

columns.name: keyword_occurrences
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of keyword occurrences for the area in the party's speeches (fct_language_area.occurrences).

columns.name: keyword_share_pct
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: area's share of the party's keyword matches, per cent 0-100; null when the party has no matches.

columns.name: attention_minus_budget
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: keyword_share_pct minus budget_share_pct, percentage points; descriptive, not a stance; adds over areas within one party and session.

columns.name: source_url
columns.description: Attribute: source URL of the party's budget proposal row.

columns.name: file_order
columns.description: Attribute: position of the row in the language audit file (fct_language_area.file_order).

nodes.sql:
-- One row per corpus, method, session, party and area where the party's budget proposal
-- covers all 27 expenditure areas: its budget share beside its lexical attention. The
-- difference in percentage points is formed at delivery (publish/export_politics.py) so it
-- rounds as the legacy build did. Descriptive only; no stance or causal inference.
with complete_frames as (
    select session, actor
    from {{ ref('fct_budget_frame') }}
    where actor <> 'GOV'
    group by session, actor
    having count(distinct expenditure_area) = 27
       and min(expenditure_area) = 1 and max(expenditure_area) = 27
)
select
    l.corpus, l.method, l.session, l.party, l.expenditure_area,
    f.budget_year, f.amount_msek, f.budget_share_pct,
    l.occurrences as keyword_occurrences, l.keyword_share_pct,
    l.keyword_share_pct - f.budget_share_pct as attention_minus_budget,
    f.source_url,
    make_date(cast(f.budget_year as integer), 1, 1) as budget_year_start,
    l.file_order
from {{ ref('fct_language_area') }} as l
join complete_frames as c on c.session = l.session and c.actor = l.party
join {{ ref('fct_budget_frame') }} as f
    on f.session = l.session and f.actor = l.party and f.expenditure_area = l.expenditure_area

nodes.name: mart_cluster_assignments
nodes.subject: clusters
nodes.description: Every published clustering's members (platform/publish/clusters): entity, period, cluster and the cluster's share of the period's assigned entities. Noise (-1) has no share.
nodes.sql:
-- One row per clustering × entity × period. Municipal clusterings take the SCB name from
-- dim_municipality; cluster_share is the cluster's share of the period's assigned entities.
with assignments as (
    select * from {{ ref('stg_cluster_assignments') }}
), named as (
    select
        a.clustering, a.entity_id,
        coalesce(m.municipality_name, a.entity_name) as entity_name,
        a.period, a.cluster, a.cluster < 0 as is_noise, a.probability
    from assignments as a
    left join {{ ref('dim_municipality') }} as m
        on m.municipality_code = a.entity_id and m.valid_to is null
        and (a.clustering like 'municipal-%' or a.clustering like 'labour-market-%')
)
select
    *,
    case when not is_noise then
        count(*) over (partition by clustering, period, cluster)
        / count(*) filter (where not is_noise) over (partition by clustering, period)
    end as cluster_share
from named

nodes.name: mart_concept_passages
nodes.subject: concepts
nodes.description: Representative chunks per concept and corpus, with provenance.

columns.name: representative_rank
columns.description: Key: rank of the chunk by z-score among the corpus's chunks where the concept is in the top three; 1 to 8.

columns.name: concept_id
columns.description: Key, references dim_concept: the concept the passage is representative for.

columns.name: corpus_id
columns.description: Key, references dim_corpus: the corpus the passage comes from.

columns.name: similarity
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: cosine similarity of the chunk to the concept's anchor sentence in the chunk's language; -1 to 1.

columns.name: rank
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: the concept's rank among all 28 concepts for this chunk; 1 to 3 here.

columns.name: z_score
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: similarity standardised against the same concept in the same corpus; standard deviations.

columns.name: chunk_id
columns.description: Foreign key to dim_text_chunk: the representative chunk.

columns.name: language
columns.description: Attribute: language of the chunk text, en or sv.

columns.name: document_id
columns.description: Attribute: id of the source document: book, philosophy work, Riksdag speech or AI Act provision.

columns.name: document_title
columns.description: Attribute: readable title of the source document.

columns.name: location

columns.name: source_url
columns.description: Attribute: URL of the source the chunk was read from.

columns.name: source_version
columns.description: Attribute: hash of the source version the chunk was read from.

columns.name: retrieved_at

columns.name: period

columns.name: text
columns.description: Attribute: the chunk text as it stands in the source.

columns.name: content_type
columns.description: Attribute: content type of the row, always 'derived'.

nodes.sql:
-- The representative chunks per concept and corpus (the concept is among the chunk's three
-- closest, ranked by z-score in the corpus), with text and provenance. What the model finds
-- closest to an anchor sentence, not a judgement that the passage is about the concept.
select
    a.concept_id,
    a.corpus_id,
    a.representative_rank,
    a.similarity,
    a.rank,
    a.z_score,
    k.chunk_id,
    k.language,
    k.document_id,
    k.document_title,
    k.location,
    k.source_url,
    k.source_version,
    k.retrieved_at,
    k.period,
    k.text,
    'derived' as content_type
from {{ ref('fct_concept_alignment') }} as a
join {{ ref('dim_text_chunk') }} as k using (chunk_id, corpus_id)
where a.representative_rank is not null

nodes.name: mart_concept_profiles
nodes.subject: concepts
nodes.description: Concept × corpus rank-1 and top-3 shares against chance (derived).

columns.name: rank1_share
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: rank1_chunks / chunks; share 0-1.

columns.name: corpus_id
columns.description: Key, references dim_corpus: the corpus.

columns.name: concept_id
columns.description: Key, references dim_concept: the concept.

columns.name: chunks
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of the corpus's chunks scored against the concept.

columns.name: rank1_chunks
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of chunks where the concept is the closest of all concepts (rank 1).

columns.name: top3_chunks
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of chunks where the concept is among the three closest concepts.

columns.name: top3_share
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: top3_chunks / chunks; share 0-1.

columns.name: rank1_chance
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: rank-1 share expected by chance, 1 / number of concepts; share 0-1.

columns.name: rank1_lift
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: rank1_share / rank1_chance; ratio, 1 means chance level.

columns.name: content_type
columns.description: Attribute: content type of the row, always 'derived'.

nodes.sql:
-- Concept × corpus: how often the concept is a chunk's closest concept (rank 1) or among its
-- three closest, against the chance share. A within-chunk comparison, so it does not depend on
-- how close a corpus's language is to anchor sentences in general. Derived.
with counts as (
    select
        corpus_id,
        concept_id,
        count(*) as chunks,
        count(*) filter (where rank = 1) as rank1_chunks,
        count(*) filter (where rank <= 3) as top3_chunks
    from {{ ref('fct_concept_alignment') }}
    group by all
),

n as (select count(*) as concepts from {{ ref('dim_concept') }})

select
    c.corpus_id,
    c.concept_id,
    c.chunks,
    c.rank1_chunks,
    c.top3_chunks,
    c.rank1_chunks / c.chunks as rank1_share,
    c.top3_chunks / c.chunks as top3_share,
    1.0 / n.concepts as rank1_chance,
    (c.rank1_chunks / c.chunks) * n.concepts as rank1_lift,
    'derived' as content_type
from counts as c cross join n

nodes.name: mart_concept_relations
nodes.subject: concepts
nodes.description: Concept × concept relations with an explicit relation type.

columns.name: relation_type
columns.description: Key: semantic_similarity (anchors among each other's three nearest in both languages) or shared_tension (editorial).

columns.name: concept_a
columns.description: Key, references dim_concept: the alphabetically first concept of the pair.

columns.name: concept_b
columns.description: Key, references dim_concept: the alphabetically second concept of the pair.

columns.name: strength
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: mean of English and Swedish anchor cosine similarity for semantic_similarity; null for shared_tension.

columns.name: tension_id
columns.description: Foreign key to dim_tension: the Philosophy Atlas tension the pair are poles of; null for semantic_similarity.

columns.name: content_type
columns.description: Attribute: content type: 'derived' for semantic_similarity, 'interpretation' for shared_tension.

nodes.sql:
-- Concept × concept relations, each with an explicit type:
-- semantic_similarity: the anchor sentences are close in both languages (each concept's three
--   nearest, kept only when the English and Swedish similarities agree on it);
-- shared_tension: the two concepts are the poles (or nearest concepts to the poles) of a
--   Philosophy Atlas tension (seeds/concepts/concept_tensions.csv), an editorial link.
with pairs as (
    select concept_a, concept_b, similarity_en, similarity_sv from {{ ref('stg_concept_similarity') }}
    union all
    select concept_b, concept_a, similarity_en, similarity_sv from {{ ref('stg_concept_similarity') }}
),

ranked as (
    select
        *,
        row_number() over (partition by concept_a order by similarity_en desc) as rank_en,
        row_number() over (partition by concept_a order by similarity_sv desc) as rank_sv
    from pairs
),

semantic as (
    select
        least(concept_a, concept_b) as concept_a,
        greatest(concept_a, concept_b) as concept_b,
        'semantic_similarity' as relation_type,
        max((similarity_en + similarity_sv) / 2) as strength,
        null as tension_id,
        'derived' as content_type
    from ranked
    where rank_en <= 3 and rank_sv <= 3
    group by all
),

tension as (
    select
        least(concept_a, concept_b) as concept_a,
        greatest(concept_a, concept_b) as concept_b,
        'shared_tension' as relation_type,
        null::double as strength,
        tension_id,
        'interpretation' as content_type
    from {{ ref('concept_tensions') }}
)

select * from semantic
union all
select * from tension

nodes.sql:
-- Model-ready features from the county panel: each measure with its value one and two years
-- earlier and its change on the year before, and the county's gap to the country in the same
-- year. Lags only look backwards, so a model predicting year t from these columns sees
-- nothing published for t. Rows are counties only; missing stays missing (no imputation).
{% set measures = ['unemployment_rate_pct', 'employment_rate_pct', 'sick_pay_rate_days',
                   'stress_cases_per_1000', 'ongoing_sick_leave_per_1000',
                   'open_unemployment_18_65_pct', 'social_assistance_pct', 'median_earned_income_sek',
                   'serious_mental_strain_pct', 'low_trust_pct'] %}
with panel as (
    select * from {{ ref('mart_county_year_panel') }}
), country as (
    select year, {% for m in measures %}{{ m }} as country_{{ m }}{{ ',' if not loop.last }}{% endfor %}
    from panel where is_country
)
select
    p.region_code,
    p.region_name,
    p.year,
    p.population,
    {% for m in measures %}
    p.{{ m }},
    lag(p.{{ m }}, 1) over w as {{ m }}_lag1,
    lag(p.{{ m }}, 2) over w as {{ m }}_lag2,
    round(p.{{ m }} - lag(p.{{ m }}, 1) over w, 4) as {{ m }}_change_1y,
    round(p.{{ m }} - c.country_{{ m }}, 4) as {{ m }}_gap_to_country{{ ',' if not loop.last }}
    {% endfor %}
from panel as p
left join country as c using (year)
where not p.is_country
-- lag() over consecutive rows equals the previous year because every county has a row for
-- every year in the panel (the panel cross-joins regions and years).
window w as (partition by p.region_code order by p.year)

nodes.sql:
-- One row per county and year with a handful of indicators side by side, for the
-- descriptive question "do regional unemployment, sick leave and self-rated health move
-- together?". It shows co-variation between counties and over time, not cause and effect:
-- counties differ in age structure, industry and much else that these columns omit.
--   unemployment_rate_pct       AKU, 15-74, annual, with its margin of error
--   sick_pay_rate_days          FK sjukpenningtal 2.0, December value (rolling 12 months), from 2021
--   stress_cases_per_1000       FK started F43 cases in the year per 1,000 inhabitants
--   serious_mental_strain_pct   Kolada N01452 (Folkhälsomyndigheten), as Kolada dates it
--   population                  SCB, 31 December
with counties as (
    select region_code, region_name from {{ ref('dim_region') }} where region_level = 'county'
), aku as (
    select region_code, cast(period_key as integer) as year, rate_pct, rate_pct_moe
    from {{ ref('fct_labour_force') }}
    where labour_status = 'unemployed' and sex_key = 'T' and length(period_key) = 4
), sick_pay as (
    select region_code, cast(left(period_key, 4) as integer) as year, sick_pay_rate
    from {{ ref('fct_sick_pay_rate') }}
    where sex_key = 'T' and age_group_key = '15-69' and right(period_key, 2) = '12'
), stress as (
    select region_code, cast(left(period_key, 4) as integer) as year,
           sum(cases) as cases, count(cases) as months_reported
    from {{ ref('fct_sick_leave_cases') }}
    where diagnosis_code = 'F43' and sex_key = 'T'
    group by all
), population as (
    select region_code, cast(period_key as integer) as year, population
    from {{ ref('fct_population') }}
    where sex_key = 'T'
), strain as (
    select region_code, cast(period_key as integer) as year, value
    from {{ ref('fct_kolada') }}
    where indicator_key = 'kolada_N01452' and sex_key = 'T'
), years as (
    select distinct year from aku
)
select
    c.region_code,
    c.region_name,
    y.year,
    a.rate_pct as unemployment_rate_pct,
    a.rate_pct_moe as unemployment_rate_moe,
    s.sick_pay_rate as sick_pay_rate_days,
    -- Only full years: a year still in progress would understate the rate.
    case when st.months_reported = 12 then round(st.cases * 1000 / p.population, 2) end
        as stress_cases_per_1000,
    m.value as serious_mental_strain_pct,
    p.population
from counties as c
cross join years as y
left join aku as a on a.region_code = c.region_code and a.year = y.year
left join sick_pay as s on s.region_code = c.region_code and s.year = y.year
left join stress as st on st.region_code = c.region_code and st.year = y.year
left join population as p on p.region_code = c.region_code and p.year = y.year
left join strain as m on m.region_code = c.region_code and m.year = y.year

nodes.sql:
-- County x year panel (plus the country as region 00) for statistical analysis: one row per
-- region and calendar year, each column aggregated by its indicator's rule in dim_indicator.
--   rates:  SCB's published annual figure, or recomputed from additive components
--   flows:  summed over the year, only when all twelve months are published
--   stocks: December for population; the mean of months for ongoing sick-leave cases
--   rolling twelve-month rates: December
-- Survey indicators pooled over four years (Folkhälsomyndigheten) sit in the row of the
-- span's last year, with the span named in fohm_period. Numerators and denominators
-- (unemployed and labour force, sick-pay days and insured) ride along so that regions can be
-- combined correctly. Descriptive: correlations between
-- counties describe counties, not people (ecological fallacy).
{% set kolada = {
    'N03937': 'open_unemployment_18_65_pct', 'N02267': 'employment_rate_20_64_pct',
    'N00938': 'sick_pay_rate_1_days', 'N00957': 'ill_health_days',
    'N00906': 'median_earned_income_sek', 'N31807': 'social_assistance_pct',
    'N07403': 'violent_crime_per_100k', 'N05403': 'turnout_riksdag_pct',
    'N01452': 'serious_mental_strain_pct', 'U01473': 'good_wellbeing_pct',
    'U01413': 'low_trust_pct', 'N15428': 'eligible_vocational_programme_pct',
} %}
{% set fohm = {
    'fohm_psy_21': 'fohm_serious_mental_strain_pct', 'fohm_psy_01': 'fohm_good_wellbeing_pct',
    'fohm_allm_01': 'fohm_good_health_pct', 'fohm_soc_40': 'fohm_hard_to_trust_pct',
} %}
with regions as (
    select region_code, region_name, county_code, nuts2_code
    from {{ ref('dim_region') }}
    where region_level in ('country', 'county')
), population as (
    select region_code, cast(period_key as integer) as year, population, is_perturbed
    from {{ ref('fct_population') }}
    where sex_key = 'T'
), aku as (
    select region_code, cast(period_key as integer) as year,
        max(rate_pct) filter (where labour_status = 'unemployed') as unemployment_rate_pct,
        max(rate_pct_moe) filter (where labour_status = 'unemployed') as unemployment_rate_moe,
        max(rate_pct) filter (where labour_status = 'employed') as employment_rate_pct,
        max(persons_thousands) filter (where labour_status = 'unemployed') as unemployed_thousands,
        max(persons_thousands) filter (where labour_status = 'employed')
            + max(persons_thousands) filter (where labour_status = 'unemployed') as labour_force_thousands
    from {{ ref('fct_labour_force') }}
    where sex_key = 'T' and age_group_key = '15-74' and series_type = 'unadjusted'
      and regexp_full_match(period_key, '\d{4}')
    group by all
), sick_pay as (
    select region_code, cast(left(period_key, 4) as integer) as year,
           sick_pay_rate as sick_pay_rate_days, sick_pay_days, insured_persons
    from {{ ref('fct_sick_pay_rate') }}
    where sex_key = 'T' and age_group_key = '15-69' and right(period_key, 2) = '12'
), stress as (
    select region_code, cast(left(period_key, 4) as integer) as year,
           case when count(cases) = 12 then sum(cases) end as stress_cases_started
    from {{ ref('fct_sick_leave_cases') }}
    where case_type = 'started' and diagnosis_code = 'F43' and sex_key = 'T'
    group by all
), ongoing as (
    select region_code, cast(left(period_key, 4) as integer) as year,
           case when count(cases) = 12 then avg(cases) end as ongoing_sick_leave_mean
    from {{ ref('fct_sick_leave_cases') }}
    where case_type = 'ongoing' and diagnosis_code = 'ALL' and sex_key = 'T' and age_group_key = '16+'
    group by all
), kolada as (
    select region_code, cast(period_key as integer) as year,
        {% for kpi, column in kolada.items() %}
        max(value) filter (where indicator_key = 'kolada_{{ kpi }}') as {{ column }}{{ ',' if not loop.last }}
        {% endfor %}
    from {{ ref('fct_kolada') }}
    where sex_key = 'T'
    group by all
), fohm as (
    select f.region_code, p.reference_year as year, any_value(f.period_key) as fohm_period,
        {% for key, column in fohm.items() %}
        max(f.share_pct) filter (where f.indicator_key = '{{ key }}') as {{ column }}{{ ',' if not loop.last }}
        {% endfor %}
    from {{ ref('fct_health_survey') }} as f
    join {{ ref('dim_period') }} as p using (period_key)
    where f.sex_key = 'T' and f.age_group_key = '16-84' and p.period_type = 'pooled_years'
    group by all
 ), years as (
    -- Years with a published AKU annual figure, the panel's backbone.
    select distinct year from aku
)
select
    r.region_code,
    r.region_name,
    r.region_code = '00' as is_country,
    r.nuts2_code,
    y.year,
    make_date(y.year, 1, 1) as year_start,
    p.population,
    p.is_perturbed as population_is_perturbed,
    a.unemployment_rate_pct,
    a.unemployment_rate_moe,
    a.employment_rate_pct,
    a.unemployed_thousands,
    a.labour_force_thousands,
    s.sick_pay_rate_days,
    s.sick_pay_days,
    s.insured_persons,
    st.stress_cases_started,
    round(1000 * st.stress_cases_started / p.population, 4) as stress_cases_per_1000,
    o.ongoing_sick_leave_mean,
    round(1000 * o.ongoing_sick_leave_mean / p.population, 4) as ongoing_sick_leave_per_1000,
    {% for column in kolada.values() %}
    k.{{ column }},
    {% endfor %}
    h.fohm_period,
    {% for column in fohm.values() %}
    h.{{ column }}{{ ',' if not loop.last }}
    {% endfor %}
from regions as r
cross join years as y
left join population as p on p.region_code = r.region_code and p.year = y.year
left join aku as a on a.region_code = r.region_code and a.year = y.year
left join sick_pay as s on s.region_code = r.region_code and s.year = y.year
left join stress as st on st.region_code = r.region_code and st.year = y.year
left join ongoing as o on o.region_code = r.region_code and o.year = y.year
left join kolada as k on k.region_code = r.region_code and k.year = y.year
left join fohm as h on h.region_code = r.region_code and h.year = y.year

nodes.name: mart_ess_country_round
nodes.subject: welfare
nodes.description: ESS weighted means per country and round, plus pooled NORDIC and EU27 groups computed from respondents with the analysis weight. Compare rounds within a country only with survey_mode in view (ESS10 self-completion).

columns.name: unit_type
columns.description: Attribute: country for a single country, group for a pooled NORDIC or EU27 row.

columns.name: unit_code
columns.description: Key: ESS two-letter country code (as in dim_country), or NORDIC or EU27 for a group.

columns.name: period_key
columns.description: Key, references dim_period: ESS round, ESSn.

columns.name: survey_mode
columns.description: Attribute: interview or self_completion for a country row; NULL for group rows.

columns.name: countries_in_unit
columns.description: Attribute: comma-separated country codes that took part in the round for this unit.

columns.name: respondents
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: distinct respondents with at least one valid answer; count of respondents; groups overlap countries.

columns.name: ppltrst_mean
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: weighted mean of ppltrst (most people can be trusted, 0-10); pspwght for countries, analysis weight for groups.

columns.name: trstprl_mean
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: weighted mean of trstprl (trust in parliament, 0-10); pspwght for countries, analysis weight for groups.

columns.name: trstplt_mean
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: weighted mean of trstplt (trust in politicians, 0-10); pspwght for countries, analysis weight for groups.

columns.name: trstplc_mean
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: weighted mean of trstplc (trust in the police, 0-10); pspwght for countries, analysis weight for groups.

columns.name: trstlgl_mean
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: weighted mean of trstlgl (trust in the legal system, 0-10); pspwght for countries, analysis weight for groups.

columns.name: stflife_mean
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: weighted mean of stflife (satisfaction with life, 0-10); pspwght for countries, analysis weight for groups.

columns.name: happy_mean
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: weighted mean of happy (how happy, 0-10); pspwght for countries, analysis weight for groups.

columns.name: stfdem_mean
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: weighted mean of stfdem (satisfaction with democracy, 0-10); pspwght for countries, analysis weight for groups.

columns.name: stfeco_mean
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: weighted mean of stfeco (satisfaction with the economy, 0-10); pspwght for countries, analysis weight for groups.

columns.name: health_mean
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: weighted mean of health (subjective general health, 1 very good to 5 very bad); pspwght for countries, analysis weight for groups.

columns.name: sclmeet_mean
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: weighted mean of sclmeet (meets friends and relatives, 1 never to 7 every day); pspwght for countries, analysis weight for groups.

columns.name: imwbcnt_mean
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: weighted mean of imwbcnt (immigrants make the country worse 0 or better 10); pspwght for countries, analysis weight for groups.

nodes.sql:
-- European Social Survey, country x round, key items side by side (weighted means with
-- pspwght, respondents), plus pooled Nordic and EU-27 rows computed from respondents with
-- the analysis weight (pspwght x pweight), as ESS's weighting guide prescribes for pooling.
-- Group composition varies by round: countries_in_unit says which took part.
{% set items = ['ppltrst', 'trstprl', 'trstplt', 'trstplc', 'trstlgl', 'stflife', 'happy',
                'stfdem', 'stfeco', 'health', 'sclmeet', 'imwbcnt'] %}
with answers as (
    select a.*, c.is_nordic, c.is_eu27
    from {{ ref('int_welfare_ess_answers') }} as a
    join {{ ref('dim_country') }} as c using (country_code)
), units as (
    select 'country' as unit_type, country_code as unit_code, * from answers
    union all
    select 'group', 'NORDIC', * from answers where is_nordic
    union all
    select 'group', 'EU27', * from answers where is_eu27
)
select
    unit_type,
    unit_code,
    period_key,
    any_value(survey_mode) filter (where unit_type = 'country') as survey_mode,
    string_agg(distinct country_code, ',' order by country_code) as countries_in_unit,
    count(distinct respondent_id || country_code) as respondents,
    {% for item in items %}
    round(sum(case when variable = '{{ item }}' then answer * (case when unit_type = 'country' then weight else pooled_weight end) end)
        / nullif(sum(case when variable = '{{ item }}' then (case when unit_type = 'country' then weight else pooled_weight end) end), 0), 6)
        as {{ item }}_mean{{ ',' if not loop.last }}
    {% endfor %}
from units
group by unit_type, unit_code, period_key

nodes.name: mart_ethics_agreement
nodes.subject: philosophy_moral
nodes.description: Gemma against the ETHICS labels per subset and wording, with the majority baseline and the label-shuffle null.

columns.name: subset
tests: accepted values: commonsense, deontology, justice, utilitarianism, virtue

nodes.sql:
-- Gemma's agreement with the ETHICS labels per subset and wording, against the majority baseline
-- and the label-shuffle null. A subset counts only when kappa beats the null in both wordings.
select
    *,
    kappa > null_kappa_p95 as beats_null,

nodes.name: mart_job_ad_municipality_field
nodes.subject: clusters
nodes.description: Distinct job ads per year, SCB municipality and occupation field, from one DuckDB pass over the JobTech cluster corpus (2023 to 2026-Q3); share within municipality and year.
nodes.sql:
-- Ads per year × municipality × occupation field, JobTech's names mapped to SCB codes through
-- the current codes of dim_municipality and the 2023 field labels harmonised through
-- occupation_field_crosswalk. share is the field's share of the municipality's ads that year.
-- Ads whose name does not map are counted in mart_job_ad_unmatched_municipalities.
with ads as (
    select a.year, a.municipality, coalesce(x.field, a.occupation_field) as occupation_field, sum(a.ads) as ads
    from {{ ref('stg_job_ad_municipality_field') }} as a
    left join {{ ref('occupation_field_crosswalk') }} as x on x.label = a.occupation_field
    group by all
)
select
    a.year, m.municipality_code, m.municipality_name, a.occupation_field, a.ads,
    a.ads / sum(a.ads) over (partition by a.year, m.municipality_code) as share
from ads as a
join {{ ref('dim_municipality') }} as m
    on m.municipality_name = a.municipality and m.valid_to is null

nodes.name: mart_job_ad_occupation_month
nodes.subject: clusters
nodes.description: Distinct job ads per publication month and occupation group.
nodes.sql:
-- Ads per month × occupation group; field is the group's occupation field, with the 2023 labels
-- harmonised through occupation_field_crosswalk. JobTech files a few groups under another field in
-- some months (Kundtjänstpersonal, Banktjänstemän, Barnskötare), so each group keeps the field
-- with the most ads over the whole period; ties go to the first field name.
with harmonised as (
    select a.month, a.occupation_group, coalesce(x.field, a.occupation_field) as occupation_field, a.ads
    from {{ ref('stg_job_ad_occupation_month') }} as a
    left join {{ ref('occupation_field_crosswalk') }} as x on x.label = a.occupation_field
),
group_field as (
    select occupation_group, first(occupation_field order by ads desc, occupation_field) as occupation_field
    from (select occupation_group, occupation_field, sum(ads) as ads from harmonised group by all)
    group by occupation_group
)
select h.month, h.occupation_group, g.occupation_field, sum(h.ads) as ads
from harmonised as h
join group_field as g using (occupation_group)
group by h.month, h.occupation_group, g.occupation_field

nodes.name: mart_job_ad_unmatched_municipalities
nodes.subject: clusters
nodes.description: JobTech municipality names with no current SCB match, and how many ads carry them.
nodes.sql:
-- Municipality names in the job ads that match no current SCB name (null: the ad has none).
select a.municipality, sum(a.ads) as ads, count(distinct a.year) as years
from {{ ref('stg_job_ad_municipality_field') }} as a
left join {{ ref('dim_municipality') }} as m
    on m.municipality_name = a.municipality and m.valid_to is null
where m.municipality_code is null
group by a.municipality

nodes.name: mart_job_ai_governance_terms
nodes.subject: job_ai_governance
nodes.description: Month × term × occupation field with denominators, rolling share and year-on-year change.

columns.name: share
columns.description: Mentions of the term / ads. Fraction from 0 to 1, not per cent.

columns.name: ads
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of ads published in the month and field, summed over archives; the denominator of share.

columns.name: term_id
columns.description: Key: term id from seeds/job_ai_governance/job_ai_governance_terms.csv.

columns.name: month
columns.description: Key: first day of the ads' publication month.

columns.name: field_id
columns.description: Key, references dim_market_field: JobTech occupation-field id; 'ALL' for the whole market; null for ads without a field.

columns.name: field
columns.description: Attribute: occupation field label; 'All occupation fields' for ALL.

columns.name: mention_count
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of ads whose headline or description matches the term; 0 when none.

columns.name: share_rolling_3m
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: mention_count / ads summed over this and the two preceding months of the series; fraction 0-1.

columns.name: share_change_yoy_pp
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: share minus share 12 rows earlier in the field and term series, on the 0-1 scale (0.01 = 1 pp); null for the first 12 months.

nodes.sql:
-- Month × term × occupation field ('ALL' for the whole market): ads mentioning the term, all
-- ads, the share, a three-month rolling share (sums over the window) and the change in share
-- against the same month a year earlier, in percentage points. A mention is a dictionary match
-- in the ad's headline or description, not a confirmed requirement.
with totals as (
    select month, field_id, field, ads from {{ ref('stg_job_gov_totals') }}
    union all
    select month, 'ALL', 'All occupation fields', sum(ads) from {{ ref('stg_job_gov_totals') }} group by month
),

hits as (
    select month, field_id, term_id, ads from {{ ref('stg_job_gov_terms') }}
    union all
    select month, 'ALL', term_id, sum(ads) from {{ ref('stg_job_gov_terms') }} group by month, term_id
),

grid as (
    select t.month, t.field_id, t.field, t.ads, k.term_id
    from totals as t
    cross join (select term_id from {{ ref('job_ai_governance_terms') }}) as k
),

joined as (
    select
        g.month,
        g.field_id,
        g.field,
        g.term_id,
        coalesce(h.ads, 0) as mention_count,
        g.ads
    from grid as g
    left join hits as h on h.month = g.month and h.field_id = g.field_id and h.term_id = g.term_id
)

select
    *,
    mention_count / ads as share,
    sum(mention_count) over w / sum(ads) over w as share_rolling_3m,
    mention_count / ads - lag(mention_count / ads, 12) over (partition by field_id, term_id order by month)
        as share_change_yoy_pp
from joined
window w as (partition by field_id, term_id order by month rows between 2 preceding and current row)

nodes.name: mart_job_ai_governance_yearly
nodes.subject: job_ai_governance
nodes.description: Year × term × field.

columns.name: share
columns.description: Mentions / ads in the year. Fraction from 0 to 1, not per cent.

columns.name: term_id
columns.description: Key: term id from seeds/job_ai_governance/job_ai_governance_terms.csv.

columns.name: year
columns.description: Key: calendar year of the ads' publication month.

columns.name: field_id
columns.description: Key, references dim_market_field: JobTech occupation-field id; 'ALL' for the whole market; null for ads without a field.

columns.name: field
columns.description: Attribute: occupation field label; 'All occupation fields' for ALL.

columns.name: mention_count
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of ads in the year whose headline or description matches the term.

columns.name: ads
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of ads published in the year and field; the denominator of share.

columns.name: months
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: count of months with ads in the year for the field, out of 12.

nodes.sql:
-- Year × term for the whole market and per occupation field: ads, mentions, share.
select
    year(month) as year,
    field_id,
    any_value(field) as field,
    term_id,
    sum(mention_count) as mention_count,
    sum(ads) as ads,
    sum(mention_count) / sum(ads) as share,
    count(*) as months
from {{ ref('mart_job_ai_governance_terms') }}
group by 1, 2, 4

-- The public ad list: every current ad and those removed in the last 30 days, without the text.
-- expired: the application deadline, a Stockholm local timestamp (JobTech gives 23:59:59), has passed.
-- rank.py applies the same rule before matching.

    employment_type, working_hours, published, changed, first_seen, application_deadline,

columns.name: ad_id

columns.name: rank

columns.name: match_class
columns.description: Attribute: strong, possible, stretch or outside, from the rules in platform/job_assistant/match.py.
tests: accepted values: strong, possible, stretch, outside

columns.name: role
columns.description: Attribute: role category, such as data_engineering or applied_ai; other when none fits.

columns.name: role_from_title
columns.description: Attribute: the role was read from the title, not only the ad text.

columns.name: reasons
columns.description: Attribute: the rules that set the class, in plain words.

columns.name: gaps
columns.description: Attribute: required or preferred skills the CV does not show in practical work or projects.

columns.name: uncertain
columns.description: Attribute: why the class may be wrong.

columns.description: Measure, non-additive: bge-m3 cosine between the ad and the profile, -1 to 1; null until embedded.

columns.description: Attribute: the sentence that mentions remote work, or null.

columns.description: Attribute: the title words that read as senior, lead or architect, or null.

columns.name: years_asked
columns.description: Attribute: the most years of experience the ad states, or null.

columns.name: junior_quote
columns.description: Attribute: the sentence that says junior, graduate or trainee, or null.

columns.name: explanation
columns.description: Attribute: the gemma explanation, only when every quote in it was found in the ad or the CV.

columns.name: explanation_status
columns.description: Attribute: verified, unverified, or null when none was made.

columns.name: explanation_model
columns.description: Attribute: the Workers AI model that wrote the explanation.

columns.name: content_hash
columns.description: Attribute: the ad version the match was made from.

columns.name: profile_version
columns.description: Attribute: the approved profile version the match used.

columns.name: cv_sha256
columns.description: Attribute: SHA-256 of the CV file behind that profile.

columns.name: engine
columns.description: Attribute: the matching rules version.

columns.name: sample
columns.description: Attribute: one of the 30 outside ads in the evaluation sample.

columns.name: detailed
columns.description: Attribute: judgements and text are published (strong, possible, stretch or sample).

nodes.sql:
-- One row per matched current ad. detailed: its judgements and text are published (the review
-- list, stretch ads and the evaluation sample); sample: one of 30 outside ads picked by a hash of
-- the id, so the owner's labels can find ads the rules missed. An ad removed or past its deadline
-- since the last match run drops out here, so no published match points at a closed ad.
with current_matches as (
    select m.*
    from {{ ref('stg_job_assistant_matches') }} as m
    inner join {{ ref('mart_job_assistant_ads') }} as a using (ad_id)
    where a.removed_at is null and not a.expired
),

sampled as (
    select ad_id
    from current_matches
    where match_class = 'outside'
    order by sha256('job-assistant-sample-v1:' || ad_id)
    limit 30
)
select
    m.ad_id, m.rank, m.match_class, m.role, m.role_from_title, m.reasons, m.gaps, m.uncertain,
    m.similarity, m.remote_quote, m.senior_title, m.years_asked, m.junior_quote,
    case when m.explanation_status = 'verified' then m.explanation end as explanation,
    m.explanation_status, m.explanation_model, m.content_hash, m.profile_version, m.cv_sha256, m.engine,
    s.ad_id is not null as sample,
    m.match_class in ('strong', 'possible', 'stretch') or s.ad_id is not null as detailed
from current_matches as m
left join sampled as s using (ad_id)

nodes.sql:
-- The record of scheduled operation: hourly runs per UTC day, how many ended well, and the ads
-- they saw as new, changed and removed.

    count(*)::integer as runs,

nodes.name: mart_job_assistant_skill_demand

nodes.description: Per skill, how many matched Data/IT ads name it and the CV's evidence level for it: how the documented experience compares with what the current ads ask for.

columns.name: skill
columns.description: Key: skill name.

columns.name: ads_required
columns.description: Measure, additive: matched ads that name the skill as required.

columns.name: ads_preferred
columns.description: Measure, additive: matched ads that name it as preferred.

columns.name: ads_naming
columns.description: Measure, additive: matched ads that name it in any way.

columns.name: share_naming
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: ads_naming / matched ads; fraction 0-1.

columns.name: cv_level
columns.description: Attribute: the CV's evidence level for the skill; null when the CV does not name it.

nodes.sql:
-- What the current Data/IT ads ask for against what the CV documents: per skill, how many matched
-- ads name it as required, preferred or in passing, and the CV's strongest evidence level for it.
with matched as (
    select count(*) as ads from {{ ref('stg_job_assistant_matches') }}
)
select
    j.skill,
    count(*) filter (where j.strength = 'required')::integer as ads_required,
    count(*) filter (where j.strength = 'preferred')::integer as ads_preferred,
    count(*)::integer as ads_naming,
    count(*) / max(matched.ads) as share_naming,
    any_value(j.cv_level) as cv_level
from {{ ref('int_job_assistant_judgements') }} as j
cross join matched
group by j.skill

nodes.name: mart_job_trends_monthly
nodes.subject: jobs
nodes.description: One row per month and role, counting distinct source advertisements. Missing coverage yields NULL official totals. Year comparisons need 12 preceding calendar months.

columns.name: ads_yoy_pct
columns.description: Change in ads from the same month a year before, as a fraction (0.05 = 5 %), despite the _pct suffix.

columns.name: ads_mom_pct
columns.description: Change in ads from the month before, as a fraction (0.05 = 5 %), despite the _pct suffix.

nodes.sql:
with counts as (
    select date_trunc('month', f.published_at)::date as publication_month,
        f.role_family, count(*) as observed_ads,
        count(distinct case when e.employer_name <> 'Unknown' then f.employer_id end) as observed_employers
    from {{ ref('fct_job_ads') }} f
    join {{ ref('dim_employer') }} e using (employer_id)
    where f.role_family <> 'Other'
    group by 1, 2
), grid as (
    select m.publication_month, r.role_family,
        coalesce(c.status = 'complete', false) as is_complete,
        coalesce(n.observed_ads, 0) as observed_ads,
        case when c.status = 'complete' then coalesce(n.observed_ads, 0) end as total_ads,
        case when c.status = 'complete' then coalesce(n.observed_employers, 0) end as unique_employers
    from {{ ref('int_analysis_months') }} m
    cross join {{ ref('role_patterns') }} r
    left join {{ ref('stg_collection_coverage') }} c using (publication_month)
    left join counts n on n.publication_month=m.publication_month and n.role_family=r.role_family
), previous as (
    select *,
        lag(total_ads) over w as previous_month_ads,
        lag(total_ads, 12) over w as previous_year_ads,
        case when count(total_ads) over w3 = 3 then avg(total_ads) over w3 end as ads_3m_average
    from grid
    window w as (partition by role_family order by publication_month),
        w3 as (partition by role_family order by publication_month rows between 2 preceding and current row)
)
select *,
    total_ads - previous_month_ads as ads_mom_change,
    total_ads::double / nullif(previous_month_ads, 0) - 1 as ads_mom_pct,
    total_ads - previous_year_ads as ads_yoy_change,
    total_ads::double / nullif(previous_year_ads, 0) - 1 as ads_yoy_pct
from previous

columns.name: field
columns.description: Attribute: the group's occupation field label in its latest month.

columns.name: ads
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of new ads, each counted once in its archive's period.

columns.name: vacancies
columns.description: Measure, additive: positions sought; an ad without a valid number of vacancies counts as one.

columns.name: ads_ytd
columns.description: Measure, additive: ads in the year's months up to the latest year's last complete month; 0 when none.

columns.name: months
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: distinct count of months with ads for the group in the year.

columns.name: ads_ytd_previous_year
columns.description: Measure, additive: ads_ytd of the group's previous row (normally the year before); NULL for its first year.

nodes.sql:
-- Ads and vacancies per occupation group and year, in full and over the same months as the
-- latest year (ads_ytd), with the change on the year before over those months.
with periods as (select * from {{ ref('int_market_periods') }}),
yearly as (
    select
        year(a.month) as year,
        a.group_id,
        sum(a.ads) as ads,
        sum(a.vacancies) as vacancies,
        sum(a.ads) filter (where month(a.month) <= p.last_month_of_latest_year) as ads_ytd,
        count(distinct a.month) as months
    from {{ ref('stg_market_ads') }} as a, periods as p
    where a.group_id is not null
    group by all
)
select
    y.year,
    y.group_id,
    g.ssyk,
    g.occupation_group,
    g.field_id,
    g.field,
    y.ads::bigint as ads,
    y.vacancies::bigint as vacancies,
    coalesce(y.ads_ytd, 0)::bigint as ads_ytd,
    y.months,
    lag(coalesce(y.ads_ytd, 0)) over (partition by y.group_id order by y.year) as ads_ytd_previous_year
from yearly as y
join {{ ref('dim_market_occupation_group') }} as g using (group_id)

-- Ads per county, occupation field and year, in full and year to date (see
-- mart_market_occupation_yearly). All fields together are in mart_market_region_yearly_total.
with periods as (select * from {{ ref('int_market_periods') }}),
base as (
    select year(a.month) as year, a.region, coalesce(a.field_id, 'unknown') as field_id,
           a.month, a.ads, a.vacancies
    from {{ ref('stg_market_ads') }} as a
), by_field as (
    select year, region, field_id,
           sum(ads) as ads, sum(vacancies) as vacancies,
           sum(ads) filter (where month(month) <= (select last_month_of_latest_year from periods)) as ads_ytd
    from base
    group by year, region, field_id
)
select
    year,
    region,
    field_id,
    ads::bigint as ads,
    vacancies::bigint as vacancies,
    coalesce(ads_ytd, 0)::bigint as ads_ytd
from by_field

nodes.sql:
-- English agreement per foundation on MFRC's test split: the tagger, the eMFD baseline and the
-- human ceiling (annotator against annotator). fairness is equality or proportionality merged,
-- the row eMFD is compared on. The intervals resample test comments (ml/moral/mfrc.py ci).
select
    foundation,
    foundation = 'fairness' as merged,
    test_comments,
    test_positives,
    tagger_f1,
    tagger_f1_low,
    tagger_f1_high,
    emfd_f1,
    tagger_vs_annotator_f1,
    human_pair_f1,
    human_alpha,
    tagger_vs_annotator_f1 / nullif(human_pair_f1, 0) as tagger_to_ceiling,
    ceiling_gap,
    ceiling_gap_low,
    ceiling_gap_high,
    c,

from {{ ref('stg_moral_agreement') }}

nodes.sql:
-- One row per municipality and year that any of the joined products covers: the welfare panel
-- (Kolada key figures and population, turnout included), the local income tax rate
-- (Skatteverket), party shares in the latest Riksdag election held by that year (SCB), public
-- libraries (SWEDEN D) and, for the clustering's reference year, SWEDEN C's frozen inputs and
-- groups (prefixed similarity_). Each product keeps its own years; a missing one is NULL.
{% set similarity = ['population', 'median_earned_income_sek', 'post_secondary_25_64_pct',
                     'group_id', 'finer_group', 'skr_group', 'pc1', 'pc2'] %}
{% set parties = ['S', 'M', 'SD', 'V', 'C', 'KD', 'MP', 'L'] %}
with panel as (
    select * from {{ ref('mart_municipality_year_panel') }}
), libraries as (
    select * from {{ ref('fct_library_municipality_year') }}
), similarity as (
    select * from {{ ref('fct_municipal_similarity') }}
), tax as (
    -- Every parish of a municipality has the same municipal and regional rate.
    select municipality_code, year, max(local_income_tax_rate) as local_income_tax_rate
    from {{ ref('fct_municipal_tax_rate') }}
    group by all
), elections as (
    select
        municipality_code, election_year,
        {% for p in parties %}
        max(share_pct) filter (where party = '{{ p }}') as share_{{ p | lower }}_pct{{ ',' if not loop.last }}
        {% endfor %}
    from {{ ref('fct_election_municipality') }}
    group by all
), spine as (
    select municipality_code, year from panel
    union
    select municipality_code, year from libraries
    union
    select municipality_code, year from similarity
    union
    select municipality_code, year from tax
)
select
    s.municipality_code,
    s.year,
    d.municipality_name,
    d.county_code,
    p.population,
    p.open_unemployment_18_65_pct,
    p.employment_rate_20_64_pct,
    p.sick_pay_rate_1_days,
    p.ill_health_days,
    p.median_earned_income_sek,
    p.social_assistance_pct,
    p.turnout_riksdag_pct,
    p.serious_mental_strain_pct,
    p.good_wellbeing_pct,
    p.low_trust_pct,
    p.eligible_vocational_programme_pct,
    t.local_income_tax_rate,
    e.election_year,
    {% for p in parties %}
    e.share_{{ p | lower }}_pct,
    {% endfor %}
    l.service_points as library_service_points,
    l.visits as library_visits,
    l.activities as library_activities,
    l.active_borrowers as library_active_borrowers,
    l.population as library_population,
    {% for c in similarity %}
    c.{{ c }} as similarity_{{ c }}{{ ',' if not loop.last }}
    {% endfor %}
from spine as s
left join {{ ref('dim_municipality') }} as d on d.municipality_code = s.municipality_code
left join panel as p on p.municipality_code = s.municipality_code and p.year = s.year
left join tax as t on t.municipality_code = s.municipality_code and t.year = s.year
asof left join elections as e on e.municipality_code = s.municipality_code and e.election_year <= s.year
left join libraries as l on l.municipality_code = s.municipality_code and l.year = s.year
left join similarity as c on c.municipality_code = s.municipality_code and c.year = s.year
