nodes.sql:
-- Sweden by month, for time-series work: labour market (seasonally adjusted and unadjusted),
-- sick-pay rate with its components, started cases with rolling twelve-month sums (a flow
-- summed over time), the psychiatric share of started cases (a ratio of two flows, formed
-- after summing), and ongoing cases (a stock: never summed over months).
with months as (
    select period_key, start_date as month_start
    from {{ ref('dim_period') }}
    where period_type = 'month'
), aku as (
    select period_key,
        max(rate_pct) filter (where labour_status = 'unemployed' and series_type = 'seasonally_adjusted') as unemployment_rate_sa,
        max(rate_pct) filter (where labour_status = 'employed' and series_type = 'seasonally_adjusted') as employment_rate_sa,
        max(rate_pct) filter (where labour_status = 'unemployed' and series_type = 'unadjusted') as unemployment_rate,
        max(rate_pct) filter (where labour_status = 'unemployed' and series_type = 'trend') as unemployment_rate_trend,
        max(persons_thousands) filter (where labour_status = 'unemployed' and series_type = 'unadjusted') as unemployed_thousands,
        max(persons_thousands) filter (where labour_status = 'labour_force' and series_type = 'unadjusted') as labour_force_thousands
    from {{ ref('fct_labour_force') }}
    where region_code = '00' and sex_key = 'T' and age_group_key = '15-74'
    group by period_key
), sick_pay as (
    select period_key, sick_pay_rate as sick_pay_rate_days, sick_pay_days, insured_persons
    from {{ ref('fct_sick_pay_rate') }}
    where region_code = '00' and sex_key = 'T' and age_group_key = '15-69'
), cases as (
    select period_key,
        max(cases) filter (where case_type = 'started' and diagnosis_code = 'ALL') as started_cases,
        max(cases) filter (where case_type = 'started' and diagnosis_code = 'F00-F99') as started_psychiatric,
        max(cases) filter (where case_type = 'started' and diagnosis_code = 'F43') as started_stress,
        max(cases) filter (where case_type = 'ongoing' and diagnosis_code = 'ALL' and age_group_key = '16+') as ongoing_cases
    from {{ ref('fct_sick_leave_cases') }}
    where region_code = '00' and sex_key = 'T'
    group by period_key
), joined as (
    select m.month_start, m.period_key, a.* exclude (period_key), s.* exclude (period_key),
           c.* exclude (period_key)
    from months as m
    left join aku as a using (period_key)
    left join sick_pay as s using (period_key)
    left join cases as c using (period_key)
)
select
    *,
    -- Rolling sums only over twelve consecutive published months.
    case when count(started_cases) over w12 = 12 then sum(started_cases) over w12 end as started_cases_12m,
    case when count(started_psychiatric) over w12 = 12 then sum(started_psychiatric) over w12 end as started_psychiatric_12m,
    case when count(started_psychiatric) over w12 = 12 and count(started_cases) over w12 = 12
         then round(100.0 * sum(started_psychiatric) over w12 / sum(started_cases) over w12, 2) end
        as psychiatric_share_of_started_12m_pct
from joined
where coalesce(unemployment_rate, sick_pay_rate_days, started_cases, ongoing_cases) is not null
window w12 as (order by month_start rows between 11 preceding and current row)

columns.name: source
columns.description: Key: the feed: svt, ekot or regeringen.

columns.description: Attribute: time of the latest fetch attempt.

columns.name: last_success
columns.description: Attribute: time of the latest fetch with no error; null when every fetch failed.

columns.name: last_status
columns.description: Attribute: HTTP status code of the latest fetch; null when the request got no response.

columns.name: last_error
columns.description: Attribute: first line of the latest fetch's error, at most 200 characters; null when it succeeded.

columns.name: fetches
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of logged fetches.

columns.name: failed_fetches
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of logged fetches with an error.

nodes.sql:
-- The latest fetch of each news source, and when it last succeeded. A fetch log in which every
-- fetch succeeded has no error key at all, so the error is read from each line as JSON
-- (null when absent) rather than as a column.
with fetches as (
    select
        source,
        cast(fetched_at as timestamptz) as fetched_at,
        status,
        to_json(f) ->> 'error' as error
    from {{ ref('stg_news_fetches') }} as f
)
select
    source,
    max(fetched_at) as last_fetch,
    max(fetched_at) filter (where error is null) as last_success,
    arg_max(status, fetched_at) as last_status,
    arg_max(error, fetched_at) as last_error,
    count(*) as fetches,
    count(*) filter (where error is not null) as failed_fetches
from fetches
group by source

columns.description: Measure, additive: count of roll calls where both parties took the same Ja or Nej position.

nodes.sql:
-- One row per session and ordered party pair (including a party with itself): of the roll
-- calls where both took a Ja or Nej position, how many had the same one. Abstentions are
-- not comparable. Not an ideological distance.
with sessions as (
    select distinct session from {{ ref('mart_vote_decisions') }}
), votes as (
    select v.* from {{ ref('stg_party_vote') }} as v join sessions using (session)
)
select
    a.session,
    a.party as party_a,
    b.party as party_b,
    count(*) filter (where a.party_position in ('Ja', 'Nej') and b.party_position in ('Ja', 'Nej')
                     and a.party_position = b.party_position) as same_position_calls,
    count(*) filter (where a.party_position in ('Ja', 'Nej') and b.party_position in ('Ja', 'Nej'))
        as comparable_calls
from votes as a
join votes as b on a.vote_id = b.vote_id
group by a.session, a.party, b.party

nodes.name: mart_party_pair_session
nodes.subject: parliament
nodes.description: Share of decisions on which two parties took the same position, per riksmöte.

columns.name: party_a
columns.description: Key, references dim_party: the alphabetically first party of the pair.

columns.name: party_b
columns.description: Key, references dim_party: the alphabetically second party of the pair.

columns.name: session
columns.description: Key, references dim_parliament_session: riksmöte, written '1993/94' or '1999/2000'.

columns.name: comparable_roll_calls
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of substantive roll calls where both parties took yes, no or abstain.

columns.name: same_position
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of those roll calls where both took the same position.

columns.name: agreement_pct
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: same_position over comparable_roll_calls; per cent 0-100, one decimal.

nodes.sql:
-- How often two parties took the same position, per riksmöte, over roll calls where both took
-- one (yes, no or abstain). The agreement matrix of the site, for every session since 1993/94.
with positions as (
    select session, roll_call_id, party, position
    from {{ ref('fct_party_roll_call') }}
    where position in ('yes', 'no', 'abstain') and is_substantive
)
select a.session, a.party as party_a, b.party as party_b,
       count(*) as comparable_roll_calls,
       count(*) filter (where a.position = b.position) as same_position,
       round(100.0 * count(*) filter (where a.position = b.position) / count(*), 1)
           as agreement_pct
from positions as a
join positions as b on a.session = b.session and a.roll_call_id = b.roll_call_id and a.party < b.party
group by a.session, a.party, b.party

nodes.name: mart_party_session_record
nodes.subject: parliament
nodes.description: Attendance, unity, winning side and voting with the government, per party and riksmöte (decisions only).

columns.name: party
columns.description: Key, references dim_party: party abbreviation (FP written L, KDS written KD).

columns.name: session
columns.description: Key, references dim_parliament_session: riksmöte, written '1993/94' or '1999/2000'.

columns.name: roll_calls
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of substantive roll calls the party is listed on in the session.

columns.name: role
columns.description: Attribute: the party's most frequent role over those roll calls: government, agreement or opposition.

columns.name: attendance_pct
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: present members over listed members, summed over roll calls; per cent 0-100.

columns.name: cohesion_pct
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: mean cohesion over roll calls; per cent 0-100.

columns.name: on_winning_side_pct
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: share of roll calls with a yes or no position that matched the outcome; per cent 0-100.

columns.name: with_government_pct
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: share of roll calls with a yes or no position that matched the prime minister's party; per cent 0-100.

columns.name: abstained_pct
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: share of roll calls where the party's position was abstain; per cent 0-100.

nodes.sql:
-- Each party's voting record per riksmöte: attendance, unity, how often it was on the winning
-- side and how often it voted with the government. Comparable across all 33 sessions.
-- Decisions only: roll calls on the reasons for a decision (motivfrågan) are left out.
select
    session, party,
    count(*) as roll_calls,
    mode(role) as role,
    round(100 * sum(present) / sum(members), 1) as attendance_pct,
    round(100 * avg(cohesion), 1) as cohesion_pct,
    round(100 * avg(case when position in ('yes', 'no') then on_winning_side::int end), 1)
        as on_winning_side_pct,
    round(100 * avg(case when position in ('yes', 'no') then with_government::int end), 1)
        as with_government_pct,
    round(100 * avg((position = 'abstain')::int), 1) as abstained_pct
from {{ ref('fct_party_roll_call') }}
where is_substantive
group by session, party

nodes.name: mart_party_session_vote
nodes.subject: politics

columns.name: party
columns.description: Key, references dim_party: party code (C, KD, L, M, MP, S, SD, V).

columns.name: session
columns.description: Key, references dim_parliament_session: riksmöte, e.g. 2024/25.

columns.name: roll_calls
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of roll calls with a vote row for the party in the session.

columns.name: yes_calls
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of roll calls where the party's position was Ja.

columns.name: no_calls
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of roll calls where the party's position was Nej.

columns.name: abstain_calls
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of roll calls where the party's position was Avstår.

columns.name: cast_member_votes
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of member votes cast (yes, no or abstain) summed over the roll calls.

columns.name: recorded_absences
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of members recorded absent summed over the roll calls; pairing unknown.

columns.name: cohesive_member_votes
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of member votes with the party's largest group (max of yes, no, abstain) summed over roll calls.

nodes.sql:
-- One row per session with roll calls and party: how often the party voted yes, no or
-- abstained as a group, and the member counts behind cohesion and recorded attendance.
-- Percentages are formed at delivery (publish/export_politics.py) so they round exactly
-- as the legacy build did.
with sessions as (
    select distinct session from {{ ref('mart_vote_decisions') }}
)
select
    v.session,
    v.party,
    count(*) as roll_calls,
    count(*) filter (where v.party_position = 'Ja') as yes_calls,
    count(*) filter (where v.party_position = 'Nej') as no_calls,
    count(*) filter (where v.party_position = 'Avstår') as abstain_calls,
    sum(v.cast_votes) as cast_member_votes,
    sum(v.absent_votes) as recorded_absences,
    sum(greatest(v.yes_votes, v.no_votes, v.abstain_votes)) as cohesive_member_votes
from {{ ref('stg_party_vote') }} as v
join sessions using (session)
group by v.session, v.party

nodes.sql:
-- One row per sampled passage and map variant (baseline, author_centered): map position,
-- cluster (-1 is noise) and membership probability, with the passage and its work. Derived.
select
    a.variant,
    a.passage_id,
    p.document_id,
    d.author,
    d.title,
    d.tradition,
    d.period,
    d.year,
    d.translator,
    p.position,
    p.text,
    a.x,
    a.y,
    a.cluster_id,
    a.probability,
    a.cluster_id = -1 as is_noise
from {{ ref('stg_philosophy_atlas') }} as a
join {{ ref('int_philosophy_passages') }} as p using (passage_id)
join {{ ref('dim_philosophy_document') }} as d on d.document_id = p.document_id

columns.name: distinctive_terms
columns.description: Attribute: JSON list of the cluster's most distinctive words by class-based TF-IDF; not a label.

columns.name: review_label
columns.description: Attribute: label written by a person reviewing the cluster; null while unreviewed, never generated.

columns.name: content_type
columns.description: Attribute: content type of the row, always 'derived'.

nodes.sql:
-- Every cluster of each map variant with its composition (works, traditions, largest-work share,
-- entropy, cross-work flag), representative passages and distinctive words, and its review
-- status. Status is 'unreviewed' unless a person has reviewed the cluster's fingerprint
-- (platform/nlp/philosophy/reviewed_clusters.json). Labels are never generated.
-- review_label is cast: while no cluster is reviewed the parquet column is all null and untyped.
select * replace (cast(review_label as varchar) as review_label), 'derived' as content_type
from {{ ref('stg_philosophy_clusters') }}

nodes.name: mart_philosophy_tension_poles
nodes.subject: philosophy
nodes.description: The passages nearest each pole of each tension.

columns.name: tension_id
columns.description: Key, references dim_tension: the tension.

columns.name: pole
columns.description: Key: which pole the passage is near: a (largest positions) or b (smallest positions).

columns.name: rank
columns.description: Key: rank of the passage towards the pole across all works; 1 to 5.

columns.name: passage_id
columns.description: Attribute: passage identifier, document_id and zero-based passage index.

columns.name: document_id
columns.description: Foreign key to dim_philosophy_document: the work the passage comes from.

columns.name: position
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: cosine similarity to pole A minus to pole B; positive leans to A.

columns.name: text
columns.description: Attribute: passage text, verbatim.

nodes.sql:
-- Per tension, the five passages closest to each pole (largest and smallest position), from
-- any work: what the lens picks out, to read against the words. Derived.
with ranked as (
    select
        s.tension_id,
        s.passage_id,
        s.position,
        p.document_id,
        p.text,
        row_number() over (partition by s.tension_id order by s.position desc) as rank_a,
        row_number() over (partition by s.tension_id order by s.position asc) as rank_b
    from {{ ref('stg_philosophy_tensions') }} as s
    join {{ ref('int_philosophy_passages') }} as p using (passage_id)
)

select tension_id, 'a' as pole, rank_a as rank, passage_id, document_id, position, text
from ranked where rank_a <= 5
union all
select tension_id, 'b', rank_b, passage_id, document_id, position, text
from ranked where rank_b <= 5

nodes.name: mart_philosophy_tensions
nodes.subject: philosophy
nodes.description: Work × tension, distribution of positions along the lens (derived).

columns.name: tension_id
columns.description: Key, references dim_tension: the tension.

columns.name: document_id
columns.description: Key, references dim_philosophy_document: the work.

columns.name: passages
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of the work's sampled passages scored on the tension.

columns.name: mean_position
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: mean position (similarity to pole A minus pole B) over the work's passages.

columns.name: q1
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: 25th percentile of position over the work's passages.

columns.name: median
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: median position over the work's passages.

columns.name: q3
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: 75th percentile of position over the work's passages.

columns.name: content_type
columns.description: Attribute: content type of the row, always 'derived'.

nodes.sql:
-- Work × tension: where a work's sampled passages sit along a lens (similarity to pole A minus
-- pole B), as mean and quartiles, and the passages nearest each pole. Derived embedding
-- similarity read through a chosen lens; not what the author holds.
with scores as (
    select s.*, p.document_id, p.text
    from {{ ref('stg_philosophy_tensions') }} as s
    join {{ ref('int_philosophy_passages') }} as p using (passage_id)
)

select
    tension_id,
    document_id,
    count(*) as passages,
    avg(position) as mean_position,
    quantile_cont(position, 0.25) as q1,
    quantile_cont(position, 0.5) as median,
    quantile_cont(position, 0.75) as q3,
    'derived' as content_type
from scores
group by tension_id, document_id

nodes.sql:
-- Product × dimension: how many checks were measured and how they came out. Counts only; no
-- score is computed, and a dimension with nothing measured says so.
select
    product_id,
    dimension,
    count(*) as check_count,
    count(*) filter (where status in ('pass', 'warning', 'fail')) as measured_count,
    count(*) filter (where status = 'pass') as pass_count,
    count(*) filter (where status = 'warning') as warning_count,
    count(*) filter (where status = 'fail') as fail_count,
    count(*) filter (where status = 'not_measured') as not_measured_count,
    count(*) filter (where status = 'not_applicable') as not_applicable_count
from {{ ref('mart_quality_checks') }}
group by all

nodes.name: mart_quality_checks

columns.name: quality_check_id

tests: accepted values: accuracy, completeness, consistency, credibility, currentness, traceability

tests: accepted values: pass, warning, fail, not_measured, not_applicable

tests: accepted values: dbt_test, python, manual_review, not_measured, not_applicable

nodes.sql:
-- One row per data-quality check result (ISO/IEC 25012-inspired dimensions). Status is pass,
-- warning, fail, not_measured or not_applicable; severity is separate. A check that measured
-- nothing is not_measured, never pass. Values are derived; the definitions are in
-- platform/quality/quality_registry.yml.
select
    quality_check_id,
    product_id,
    project_id,
    dataset_id,
    dimension,
    dimension_label,
    description,
    measure_name,
    numerator_definition,
    denominator_definition,
    comparator,
    threshold,
    warn_at,
    value,
    numerator,
    denominator,
    sample_size,
    reviewed_at,
    status,
    severity,
    method,
    source,
    gate,
    details,
    evaluated_at::timestamptz as evaluated_at,
    'derived' as content_type
from {{ ref('stg_quality_checks') }}

nodes.name: mart_skill_trends_monthly
nodes.subject: jobs
nodes.description: One row per month, role and technology. Counts, distinct known employers, shares, calendar-aligned growth and weighted three-month shares. total_ads is repeated per skill and must not be summed across skills.

columns.name: skill_ads_yoy_pct
columns.description: Change in ads with the skill from the same month a year before, as a fraction (0.05 = 5 %), despite the _pct suffix.

columns.name: skill_ads_mom_pct
columns.description: Change in ads with the skill from the month before, as a fraction (0.05 = 5 %), despite the _pct suffix.

columns.name: previous_year_share
columns.description: skill_share of the same month a year before. Fraction from 0 to 1, not per cent.

columns.name: previous_month_share
columns.description: skill_share of the month before. Fraction from 0 to 1, not per cent.

columns.name: skill_share
columns.description: Ads with the skill / all ads of the role family in the month. Fraction from 0 to 1, not per cent.

columns.name: sufficient_volume
columns.description: At least 20 cohort ads and five skill mentions by default; descriptive threshold, not statistical significance.

nodes.sql:
with counts as (
    select date_trunc('month', f.published_at)::date as publication_month,
        f.role_family, s.skill, count(distinct f.job_id) as observed_skill_ads,
        count(distinct case when e.employer_name <> 'Unknown' then f.employer_id end) as observed_skill_employers
    from {{ ref('fct_job_ads') }} f
    join {{ ref('bridge_job_skills') }} s using (job_id)
    join {{ ref('dim_employer') }} e using (employer_id)
    where f.role_family <> 'Other'
    group by 1, 2, 3
), grid as (
    select j.publication_month, j.role_family, s.skill, j.is_complete, j.total_ads,
        case when j.is_complete then coalesce(n.observed_skill_ads, 0) end as ads_with_skill,
        case when j.is_complete then coalesce(n.observed_skill_employers, 0) end as unique_employers
    from {{ ref('mart_job_trends_monthly') }} j
    cross join {{ ref('technology_patterns') }} s
    left join counts n on n.publication_month=j.publication_month
        and n.role_family=j.role_family and n.skill=s.skill
), shares as (
    select *, ads_with_skill::double / nullif(total_ads, 0) as skill_share
    from grid
), previous as (
    select *, lag(ads_with_skill) over w as previous_month_skill_ads,
        lag(ads_with_skill, 12) over w as previous_year_skill_ads,
        lag(skill_share) over w as previous_month_share,
        lag(skill_share, 12) over w as previous_year_share,
        case when count(ads_with_skill) over w3 = 3
            then sum(ads_with_skill) over w3 / nullif(sum(total_ads) over w3, 0) end as skill_share_3m,
        case when total_ads >= {{ var('minimum_cohort_ads', 20) }} and ads_with_skill >= 5
            then true else false end as sufficient_volume
    from shares
    window w as (partition by role_family, skill order by publication_month),
        w3 as (partition by role_family, skill order by publication_month rows between 2 preceding and current row)
)
select *,
    ads_with_skill::double / nullif(previous_month_skill_ads, 0) - 1 as skill_ads_mom_pct,
    ads_with_skill::double / nullif(previous_year_skill_ads, 0) - 1 as skill_ads_yoy_pct,
    100 * (skill_share - previous_month_share) as share_mom_pp,
    100 * (skill_share - previous_year_share) as share_yoy_pp
from previous

nodes.name: mart_skill_year_comparison
nodes.subject: jobs
nodes.description: One row per role and technology comparing complete baseline/comparison years. Annual shares use counts, not averages of monthly percentages.
nodes.sql:
with annual as (
    select year(publication_month) as publication_year, role_family, skill,
        count(*) filter (where is_complete) as complete_months,
        sum(ads_with_skill) as skill_ads, sum(total_ads) as total_ads
    from {{ ref('mart_skill_trends_monthly') }}
    group by 1, 2, 3
)
select a.role_family, a.skill,
    {{ var('baseline_year', 2024) }} as baseline_year,
    {{ var('comparison_year', 2025) }} as comparison_year,
    a.complete_months = 12 and b.complete_months = 12 as is_complete,
    case when a.complete_months = 12 then a.skill_ads end as baseline_skill_ads,
    case when a.complete_months = 12 then a.total_ads end as baseline_total_ads,
    case when b.complete_months = 12 then b.skill_ads end as comparison_skill_ads,
    case when b.complete_months = 12 then b.total_ads end as comparison_total_ads,
    case when a.complete_months = 12 and b.complete_months = 12 then
        100 * (b.skill_ads / nullif(b.total_ads, 0) - a.skill_ads / nullif(a.total_ads, 0))
    end as share_change_pp
from annual a
left join annual b on a.role_family=b.role_family and a.skill=b.skill
    and b.publication_year={{ var('comparison_year', 2025) }}
where a.publication_year={{ var('baseline_year', 2024) }}

nodes.name: mart_sweden_future_lengths
nodes.subject: sweden_futures
nodes.description: The Lost Futures. Year × words in the speech over all Riksdag speeches; the export cuts it into fixed length bands (quartiles of the published years) to compare the future share at equal length.

columns.name: year
columns.description: Key: calendar year of the speeches.

columns.name: words
columns.description: Key: words in the speech; speeches above the ingest cap (MAX_WORDS) share its value.

columns.name: speeches
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of Riksdag speeches of this length.

columns.name: future_speeches

nodes.sql:
-- The Lost Futures: calendar year × words in the speech over all Riksdag speeches, so the future
-- share can be compared within fixed length bands. Speeches above the ingest's cap share its bin.
select try_cast(year as integer) as year, words,
       sum(speeches) as speeches, sum(future) as future_speeches
from {{ ref('stg_futures_lengths') }}
where try_cast(year as integer) is not null
group by all

nodes.name: mart_sweden_future_subterms
nodes.subject: sweden_futures
nodes.description: Year × sub-term of the security and culture themes (seed future_subterms) over all Riksdag speeches. The sub-terms split each theme's pattern, so their matches add up to the theme's.

columns.name: year
columns.description: Key, references mart_sweden_future_trends_total: calendar year of the speeches.

columns.name: theme
columns.description: The future_terms theme the sub-term splits.

columns.description: Key: future_subterms term id.

columns.description: Measure, additive: count of speeches using the sub-term; adds over years, not sub-terms.

columns.description: Measure, additive: count of future-oriented speeches using the sub-term; adds over years, not sub-terms.

columns.name: matches
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of sub-term pattern matches; adds over sub-terms to the theme's matches.

columns.name: future_share_using
columns.description: Non-additive ratio: future-oriented speeches using the sub-term / future-oriented speeches.

nodes.sql:
-- Year × sub-term of the security and culture themes (future_subterms) across all parties. Each
-- share is over the year's future-oriented speeches (mart_sweden_future_trends_total).
with hits as (
    select try_cast(year as integer) as year, theme as subterm,
           sum(speeches) as speeches_using, sum(future) as future_using, sum(matches) as matches
    from {{ ref('stg_futures_hits') }}
    group by all
)

select
    y.year, s.theme, s.term_id as subterm,
    coalesce(h.speeches_using, 0) as speeches_using,
    coalesce(h.future_using, 0) as future_using,
    coalesce(h.matches, 0) as matches,
    coalesce(h.future_using, 0) / nullif(y.future_speeches, 0) as future_share_using
from {{ ref('mart_sweden_future_trends_total') }} as y
cross join {{ ref('future_subterms') }} as s
left join hits as h on h.year = y.year and h.subterm = s.term_id

nodes.name: mart_sweden_future_themes
nodes.subject: sweden_futures
nodes.description: The Lost Futures. Year × party × theme over Riksdag speeches, per-theme counts only; join mart_sweden_future_totals on year and party for the speeches and words.

columns.name: year
columns.description: Key: calendar year of the speeches; a year sums its autumn and spring sessions.

columns.name: party
columns.description: Key, references dim_party: party code (KDS as KD); NULL for the Speaker's, the King's and the ålderspresident's roles and speeches with no party.

columns.name: theme
columns.description: Key: future_terms theme id (family theme).

columns.name: speeches_using
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of speeches using the theme, 0 when none; adds over years and parties, not themes.

columns.name: future_using
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of future-oriented speeches using the theme, 0 when none; adds over years and parties, not themes.

columns.name: matches
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of theme pattern matches in the speeches, 0 when none.

nodes.sql:
-- The Lost Futures: calendar year × party × theme in Riksdag speeches. Only the per-theme counts;
-- the speeches, words and marker matches of a year and party are in mart_sweden_future_totals,
-- once per cell. Every theme gets a row for every year and party, zero when unused.
with hits as (
    select try_cast(year as integer) as year,
           -- KDS is KD (parliament_party); the Speaker's, the King's and the ålderspresident's
           -- roles and a missing party have no party: null.
           case when not regexp_matches(upper(party), 'TALMAN|PRESIDENT|KONUNG')
                then {{ parliament_party('party') }} end as party, theme,
           sum(speeches) as speeches_using, sum(future) as future_using, sum(matches) as matches
    from {{ ref('stg_futures_hits') }}
    group by all
)

select
    t.year, t.party, c.term_id as theme,
    coalesce(h.speeches_using, 0) as speeches_using,
    coalesce(h.future_using, 0) as future_using,
    coalesce(h.matches, 0) as matches
from {{ ref('mart_sweden_future_totals') }} t
cross join (select term_id from {{ ref('future_terms') }} where family = 'theme') c
left join hits h on h.year = t.year and h.party is not distinct from t.party and h.theme = c.term_id

nodes.name: mart_sweden_future_theses
nodes.subject: sweden_futures
nodes.description: Year × theme over Swedish-language student-thesis abstracts in DiVA, never pooled with the Riksdag; join mart_sweden_future_theses_total on year for the abstracts and words.

columns.name: future_share_using
columns.description: Non-additive ratio: future-oriented abstracts using the theme / future-oriented abstracts.

columns.name: per_1000_words
columns.description: Non-additive ratio: theme matches per thousand words.

columns.name: year
columns.description: Key, references mart_sweden_future_theses_total: publication year of the abstracts.

columns.name: theme
columns.description: Key: future_terms theme id (family theme).

columns.name: abstracts_using
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of thesis abstracts using the theme, 0 when none; adds over years, not themes.

columns.name: future_using
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of future-oriented abstracts using the theme, 0 when none; adds over years, not themes.

columns.name: matches
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of theme pattern matches in the abstracts, 0 when none.

nodes.sql:
-- The academic corpus of The Lost Futures: publication year × theme in Swedish-language
-- student-thesis abstracts. Kept apart from the Riksdag marts: another genre, other authors.
-- Each record counts once, at its latest harvested month (int_sweden_future_theses_latest). The
-- abstracts and words of a year are in mart_sweden_future_theses_total.
with cells as (
    select year::integer as year, theme,
           count(*) as abstracts, count(*) filter (where future) as future,
           sum(matches) as matches
    from {{ ref('int_sweden_future_theses_latest') }}
    where year is not null and theme <> '_all'
    group by all
)

select
    t.year, c.term_id as theme,
    coalesce(x.abstracts, 0) as abstracts_using,
    coalesce(x.future, 0) as future_using,
    coalesce(x.matches, 0) as matches,
    coalesce(x.future, 0) / nullif(t.future_abstracts, 0) as future_share_using,
    coalesce(x.matches, 0) * 1000.0 / nullif(t.words, 0) as per_1000_words
from {{ ref('mart_sweden_future_theses_total') }} as t
cross join (select term_id from {{ ref('future_terms') }} where family = 'theme') as c
left join cells as x on x.year = t.year and x.theme = c.term_id

nodes.sql:
-- The DiVA 2024-25 jump taken apart: publication year × degree level × HSV subject area ×
-- institution over Swedish-language student-thesis abstracts harvested from record month 2019-01,
-- with the abstracts using each alternative of the future marker. `future_without_research`
-- counts abstracts that still match the marker once "framtida forskning" and its kin are dropped;
-- `future_without_research_long_term` also drops "långsiktig" and "på lång sikt".
select
    year::integer as year, level, area, institution,
    count(*) as abstracts,
    count(*) filter (where m_research + m_framtiden + m_framtida + m_framtid_compound
                           + m_long_term + m_vision + m_other > 0) as future_abstracts,
    count(*) filter (where m_framtiden + m_framtida + m_framtid_compound
                           + m_long_term + m_vision + m_other > 0) as future_without_research,
    count(*) filter (where m_framtiden + m_framtida + m_framtid_compound
                           + m_vision + m_other > 0) as future_without_research_long_term,
    count(*) filter (where m_research > 0) as using_research,
    count(*) filter (where m_framtiden > 0) as using_framtiden,
    count(*) filter (where m_framtida > 0) as using_framtida,
    count(*) filter (where m_framtid_compound > 0) as using_framtid_compound,
    count(*) filter (where m_long_term > 0) as using_long_term,
    count(*) filter (where m_vision > 0) as using_vision,
    count(*) filter (where m_other > 0) as using_other,
    sum(words) as words
from {{ ref('int_sweden_future_theses_detail_latest') }}
where year is not null
group by all

-- The futures topic pilot per cluster × corpus: unreviewed label, c-TF-IDF top terms, stability,
-- the share's linear trend (permutation p, Holm over stable cluster × corpus tests) and, per
-- cluster, the Riksdag-DiVA correlation of differenced yearly shares at lag 0 and at the strongest
-- lag in -3..+3 (Holm over clusters). corpus_specific: 90 % or more of its sentences from one corpus,
-- so never evidence that the corpora share a future. Exploratory until the clusters are reviewed.
select

    sentences, corpus_sentences, share_mean, trend_slope, trend_p, trend_p_holm,

nodes.sql:
-- The futures topic pilot: year × corpus × unsupervised cluster of sampled future-marked sentences
-- (Riksdag speeches and Swedish DiVA abstracts, one sentence per document, at most 1,500 a year per
-- corpus). Cluster -1 is noise and stays in the denominator. Labels stay "unreviewed cluster N"
-- until the owner has reviewed them; the corpora share one embedding space but are never pooled.
with counted as (
    select corpus, year::integer as year, cluster::integer as cluster, count(*) as sentences
    from {{ ref('stg_futures_topics') }}
    group by all
), totals as (
    select corpus, year, sum(sentences) as year_sentences from counted group by all
), labels as (
    -- One row per cluster: the per-corpus rows repeat the cluster's label, terms and stability.
    select cluster::integer as cluster, label, top_terms, stable from {{ ref('stg_futures_topic_clusters') }}
    qualify row_number() over (partition by cluster order by corpus) = 1
)

select
    c.year::integer as year, c.corpus, c.cluster::integer as cluster,
    coalesce(l.label, 'noise') as label, l.top_terms, coalesce(l.stable, false) as stable,
    coalesce(n.sentences, 0) as sentences, t.year_sentences,
    coalesce(n.sentences, 0) / t.year_sentences as share,
    c.share_low, c.share_high, c.run_id
from {{ ref('stg_futures_topic_cells') }} as c
join totals as t on t.corpus = c.corpus and t.year = c.year
left join counted as n on n.corpus = c.corpus and n.year = c.year and n.cluster = c.cluster
left join labels as l on l.cluster = c.cluster

nodes.sql:
-- The Lost Futures: calendar year × party over all Riksdag speeches. Sessions straddle calendar
-- years, so a year sums its autumn and spring. `marker_matches` is null for a cell until every
-- session in it was counted with the column. Per-theme counts are in mart_sweden_future_themes.
select try_cast(year as integer) as year,
       -- KDS is KD (parliament_party); the Speaker's, the King's and the ålderspresident's
       -- roles and a missing party have no party: null.
       case when not regexp_matches(upper(party), 'TALMAN|PRESIDENT|KONUNG')
            then {{ parliament_party('party') }} end as party,
       sum(speeches) as speeches, sum(future) as future_speeches, sum(words) as words,
       case when count(marker_matches) = count(*) then sum(marker_matches) end as marker_matches
from {{ ref('stg_futures_totals') }}
where try_cast(year as integer) is not null
group by all

-- Year × theme across all parties: which futures the chamber speaks of. Each rate is over
-- speeches of that year (mart_sweden_future_trends_total); nothing is pooled across corpora.
with themes as (
    select year, theme,
           sum(speeches_using) as speeches_using,
           sum(future_using) as future_using,
           sum(matches) as matches
    from {{ ref('mart_sweden_future_themes') }}
    group by year, theme
)

select
    t.year, t.theme, t.speeches_using, t.future_using, t.matches,
    t.future_using / nullif(y.future_speeches, 0) as future_share_using,
    t.matches * 1000.0 / nullif(y.words, 0) as per_1000_words
from themes as t
join {{ ref('mart_sweden_future_trends_total') }} as y using (year)

-- speeches of the year. The per-theme counts are in mart_sweden_future_trends.

    sum(speeches) as speeches,
    sum(future_speeches) as future_speeches,
    sum(words) as words,

nodes.sql:
-- The Ideal Human: year × occupation field × county × category. Only the per-category counts;
-- the ads, distinct texts and words of a cell are in mart_sweden_job_language_totals, once per
-- cell. Every category gets a row for every cell, zero when unused. Fields go through the same
-- crosswalk as the totals.
with hits as (
    select try_cast(year as integer) as year, coalesce(x.field, h.field, 'Unknown') as field,
           coalesce(region, 'Unknown') as region, category,
           sum(texts) as texts_matching, sum(matches) as matches
    from {{ ref('stg_ad_language_hits') }} h
    left join {{ ref('occupation_field_crosswalk') }} x on x.label = h.field
    group by all
)

select
    t.year, t.field, t.region, c.term_id as category, c.family,
    coalesce(h.texts_matching, 0) as texts_matching,
    coalesce(h.matches, 0) as matches
from {{ ref('mart_sweden_job_language_totals') }} t
cross join {{ ref('ad_language_terms') }} c
left join hits h
    on h.year = t.year and h.field = t.field and h.region = t.region and h.category = c.term_id

nodes.sql:
-- The Ideal Human by ad length: year × occupation field × length band × category, nationally,
-- for the categories of ad_language_terms and their sub-terms (ad_language_subterms). The four
-- bands are cut at the 2010 quartiles of words per distinct text (BANDS in ad_language.py), so a
-- year can be compared with itself at the lengths ads had in 2010. Every category gets a row for
-- every cell, zero when unused. Feature files counted before the bands existed have no band and
-- are left out.
with totals as (
    select try_cast(year as integer) as year, coalesce(x.field, t.field, 'Unknown') as field, band,
           sum(distinct_texts) as texts, sum(words) as words
    from {{ ref('stg_ad_language_totals') }} t
    left join {{ ref('occupation_field_crosswalk') }} x on x.label = t.field
    where try_cast(year as integer) is not null and band is not null
    group by all
),

hits as (
    select try_cast(year as integer) as year, coalesce(x.field, h.field, 'Unknown') as field, band,
           category, sum(texts) as texts_matching, sum(matches) as matches
    from {{ ref('stg_ad_language_hits') }} h
    left join {{ ref('occupation_field_crosswalk') }} x on x.label = h.field
    where band is not null
    group by all
),

categories as (
    select term_id as category, term_id as parent from {{ ref('ad_language_terms') }}
    union all
    select term_id, parent from {{ ref('ad_language_subterms') }}
)

select
    t.year, t.field, t.band, c.category, c.parent, t.texts, t.words,
    coalesce(h.texts_matching, 0) as texts_matching,
    coalesce(h.matches, 0) as matches
from totals t
cross join categories c
left join hits h
    on h.year = t.year and h.field = t.field and h.band = t.band and h.category = c.category

nodes.subject: sweden_language
nodes.description: Year × category (terms and sub-terms) nationally in three measures with the occupation mix fixed: share of texts, matches per thousand words, and share of texts within 2010 length bands. A change is read as stable only when the three agree in sign.

columns.name: year
columns.description: Key: publication year of the job ads.

columns.name: category
columns.description: Key: ad_language_terms category id, or an ad_language_subterms id.

columns.name: parent
columns.description: Attribute: the category itself, or the parent category of a sub-term.

columns.name: texts
columns.description: Measure, additive over years: count of distinct ad texts.

columns.name: words
columns.description: Measure, additive over years: words of the distinct texts.

columns.name: texts_matching
columns.description: Measure, additive over years: count of distinct texts using the category.

columns.name: matches
columns.description: Measure, additive over years: count of pattern matches.

columns.name: share
columns.description: Non-additive ratio: texts using the category / distinct texts.

columns.name: per_1000_words
columns.description: Non-additive ratio: matches per thousand words.

columns.name: share_standardised
columns.description: Non-additive ratio: the share with the occupation-field mix fixed.

columns.name: per_1000_words_standardised
columns.description: Non-additive ratio: matches per thousand words with the occupation-field mix fixed.

columns.name: share_banded_standardised
columns.description: Non-additive ratio: the share within each 2010 length band, combined with 2010 band weights and the fixed occupation-field mix.

nodes.sql:
-- Year × category (terms and sub-terms), nationally, in three measures with the occupation mix
-- fixed at its pooled share as in mart_sweden_job_language_trends: the share of texts using the
-- category, matches per thousand words, and the share of texts within each 2010 length band,
-- combined with the band weights of 2010. Longer ads raise the first, and a requirement stated
-- once per ad lowers the second as ads grow; the third holds length at its 2010 distribution.
-- A change is read as stable only when all three agree in sign. The same rules as the trends
-- mart apply: a field-year (or field-year-band) cell needs 30 distinct texts, and a year where
-- fewer than half the texts have a field gets no standardised value.
with cells as (
    select * from {{ ref('mart_sweden_job_language_bands') }}
),

field_year as (
    select year, field, category, any_value(parent) as parent,
           sum(texts) as texts, sum(words) as words,
           sum(texts_matching) as texts_matching, sum(matches) as matches
    from cells
    group by all
),

weights as (
    select field, sum(texts) / sum(sum(texts)) over () as weight
    from field_year
    where category = 'competence' and field <> 'Unknown'
    group by field
),

band_weights as (
    select band, sum(texts) / sum(sum(texts)) over () as weight
    from cells
    where year = 2010 and category = 'competence'
    group by band
),

standardised as (
    select f.year, f.category,
           sum(f.texts) as known_texts,
           sum(w.weight * f.texts_matching / f.texts) filter (where f.texts >= 30)
               / nullif(sum(w.weight) filter (where f.texts >= 30), 0) as share,
           sum(w.weight * f.matches * 1000.0 / f.words) filter (where f.texts >= 30 and f.words > 0)
               / nullif(sum(w.weight) filter (where f.texts >= 30 and f.words > 0), 0) as per_1000_words
    from field_year f
    join weights w using (field)
    group by all
),

banded as (
    select c.year, c.category,
           sum(w.weight * b.weight * c.texts_matching / c.texts) filter (where c.texts >= 30)
               / nullif(sum(w.weight * b.weight) filter (where c.texts >= 30), 0) as share
    from cells c
    join weights w using (field)
    join band_weights b using (band)
    group by all
),

national as (
    select year, category, any_value(parent) as parent,
           sum(texts) as texts, sum(words) as words,
           sum(texts_matching) as texts_matching, sum(matches) as matches
    from field_year
    group by all
)

select
    n.year, n.category, n.parent, n.texts, n.words, n.texts_matching, n.matches,
    n.texts_matching / nullif(n.texts, 0) as share,
    n.matches * 1000.0 / nullif(n.words, 0) as per_1000_words,
    case when s.known_texts >= 0.5 * n.texts then s.share end as share_standardised,
    case when s.known_texts >= 0.5 * n.texts then s.per_1000_words end as per_1000_words_standardised,
    case when s.known_texts >= 0.5 * n.texts then b.share end as share_banded_standardised
from national n
left join standardised s using (year, category)
left join banded b using (year, category)

columns.description: Non-additive ratio: matches per thousand words of the distinct texts.

columns.name: per_1000_words_standardised
columns.description: Non-additive ratio: matches per thousand words with the occupation-field mix fixed.

columns.name: known_field_share
columns.description: Non-additive ratio: distinct texts with an occupation field / all distinct texts.

columns.name: year
columns.description: Key: publication year of the job ads.

columns.name: category
columns.description: Key: ad_language_terms category id.

columns.name: family
columns.description: Attribute: the category's family from ad_language_terms (such as skill or personal).

columns.name: texts
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of distinct ad texts in the year, all fields and counties; adds over years, not categories.

columns.name: words
columns.description: Measure, additive: words of the year's distinct ad texts; count of words.

columns.name: texts_matching
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of distinct texts using the category; adds over years, not categories.

columns.name: matches
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of category pattern matches in the year's distinct texts.

nodes.sql:
-- Year × category, nationally. `share` is the crude share of distinct ad texts that use the
-- category; `share_standardised` holds the occupation mix fixed at its pooled share of all
-- years (direct standardisation), so a change in which jobs are advertised does not read as a
-- change in language. `per_1000_words` is matches per thousand words, and
-- `per_1000_words_standardised` the same with the occupation mix fixed: ads grew several times
-- longer since 2006, so shares of ads rise with length alone and rates per word are the fairer
-- comparison over time. Texts without an occupation field take no part in the standardisation,
-- and a year where fewer than half the texts have one gets no standardised value (the 2006
-- archive records no occupation at all). A field-year with fewer than 30 distinct texts takes
-- no part either: a handful of texts would otherwise carry the field's full weight.
with field_year as (
    select year, field, category, family,
           sum(texts) as texts, sum(words) as words,
           sum(texts_matching) as texts_matching, sum(matches) as matches
    from {{ ref('mart_sweden_job_language') }}
    join {{ ref('mart_sweden_job_language_totals') }} using (year, field, region)
    group by all
),

weights as (
    select field, sum(texts) / sum(sum(texts)) over () as weight
    from field_year
    where category = 'competence' and field <> 'Unknown'
    group by field
),

standardised as (
    select f.year, f.category,
           sum(f.texts) / any_value(t.texts) as known_share,
           sum(w.weight * f.texts_matching / f.texts) filter (where f.texts >= 30)
               / nullif(sum(w.weight) filter (where f.texts >= 30), 0) as share,
           sum(w.weight * f.matches * 1000.0 / f.words) filter (where f.texts >= 30 and f.words > 0)
               / nullif(sum(w.weight) filter (where f.texts >= 30 and f.words > 0), 0) as per_1000_words
    from field_year f
    join weights w using (field)
    join (select year, category, sum(texts) as texts from field_year group by all) t
        using (year, category)
    group by f.year, f.category
)

select
    f.year, f.category, any_value(f.family) as family,
    sum(f.texts) as texts,
    sum(f.words) as words,
    sum(f.texts_matching) as texts_matching,
    sum(f.matches) as matches,
    sum(f.texts_matching) / nullif(sum(f.texts), 0) as share,
    sum(f.matches) * 1000.0 / nullif(sum(f.words), 0) as per_1000_words,
    any_value(case when s.known_share >= 0.5 then s.share end) as share_standardised,
    any_value(case when s.known_share >= 0.5 then s.per_1000_words end) as per_1000_words_standardised,
    coalesce(any_value(s.known_share), 0) as known_field_share
from field_year f
left join standardised s using (year, category)
group by f.year, f.category

nodes.name: mart_sweden_measurement_coverage
nodes.subject: sweden
nodes.description: Domain × year × finest geography, counting SCB tables whose period range covers the year (upper bound).

columns.name: tables
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of public SCB tables whose period range covers the year, an upper bound; adds over domains and geographies, not years.

columns.name: domain_id
columns.description: Key: research domain id from seeds/sweden (research_domains).

columns.name: year
columns.description: Key: calendar year inside the tables' first to last period.

columns.name: geo_resolution
columns.description: Key: finest geography of the tables: national, county, municipality or subarea.

nodes.sql:
-- Domain × year: how many SCB tables report each year, at which finest geography. A table
-- covers every year from its first to its last period; gaps inside a series are not visible
-- in the catalogue, so this is an upper bound. Kolada has no first year in its catalogue and
-- is left out.
with years as (
    select unnest(range(1900, extract(year from current_date)::integer + 1)) as year
)
select
    i.domain_id,
    y.year,
    i.geo_resolution,
    count(*) as tables
from {{ ref('mart_sweden_measurement_items') }} i
join years y on y.year between i.first_year and i.last_year
where i.catalogue = 'scb'
group by all

nodes.name: mart_sweden_measurement_items
nodes.subject: sweden
nodes.description: Politics of Measurement. One row per public SCB table and Kolada key figure, with the research domain from seeds/sweden, period range, frequency and finest geography.

columns.name: domain_id
columns.description: Every subject must be classified; a new SCB subject fails this test.

columns.name: geo_resolution
columns.description: Attribute: finest geography by the region codes reported: national, county, municipality or subarea; Kolada county or municipality.
tests: accepted values: national, county, municipality, subarea

columns.name: last_year
columns.description: SCB only; Kolada's catalogue has no period range.

columns.name: is_current
columns.description: SCB last period within two years; Kolada a scheduled publication.

columns.name: catalogue
columns.description: Key: source catalogue: scb or kolada.

columns.name: item_id
columns.description: Key: SCB table id or Kolada key figure id (kpi_id).

columns.name: title
columns.description: Attribute: table or key figure title as the catalogue gives it (Swedish).

columns.name: institution
columns.description: Attribute: producing institution; for Kolada the source named in the description, else Kolada (RKA).

columns.name: subject_code
columns.description: Attribute: SCB second-level subject code, or Kolada's operating area.

columns.name: subject_label
columns.description: Attribute: SCB second-level subject label, or Kolada's operating area.

columns.name: frequency
columns.description: Attribute: publication frequency: month, quarter or year (other SCB time units lower-cased); Kolada always year.

columns.name: first_year
columns.description: Attribute: year of the SCB table's first period; NULL for Kolada, whose catalogue has no period range.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.description: Attribute: when SCB last updated the table; NULL for Kolada.

columns.name: measures
columns.description: Measure, additive: contents (metric categories) in the SCB table's metadata; NULL for Kolada and for SCB tables without a region variable, whose metadata is not fetched.

nodes.sql:
-- Politics of Measurement: one row per published statistical table (SCB) or key figure
-- (Kolada), classified into the research domains by seeds/sweden/*_domains.csv. Counting
-- these describes what official statistics publish; it says nothing about how important a
-- domain is, and one table is not one indicator.
with scb as (
    select
        t.*,
        coalesce(sub.domain_id, area.domain_id) as domain_id,
        g.region_codes, g.county_codes, g.municipality_codes, g.subarea_codes, g.measures
    from {{ ref('stg_sweden_scb_tables') }} t
    left join {{ ref('scb_subject_domains') }} sub on sub.subject_code = t.subject_code
    left join {{ ref('scb_subject_domains') }} area on area.subject_code = t.subject_area
    left join {{ ref('stg_sweden_scb_geography') }} g using (table_id)
    where t.is_public
),

kolada as (
    select
        k.*,
        case
            when a.domain_id = 'culture'
                 and regexp_matches(lower(k.title), 'idrott|fritid|motion|simhall|badhus|friluft')
                then 'leisure'
            else a.domain_id
        end as domain_id
    from {{ ref('stg_sweden_kolada_kpis') }} k
    left join {{ ref('kolada_area_domains') }} a using (operating_area)
)

select
    'scb' as catalogue,
    table_id as item_id,
    title,
    institution,
    subject_code,
    subject_label,
    domain_id,
    case time_unit
        when 'Monthly' then 'month' when 'Quarterly' then 'quarter'
        when 'Annual' then 'year' else lower(time_unit)
    end as frequency,
    first_year,
    last_year,
    case
        when subarea_codes >= 50 then 'subarea'
        when municipality_codes >= 200 then 'municipality'
        when county_codes >= 15 then 'county'
        else 'national'
    end as geo_resolution,
    last_year >= extract(year from current_date) - 2 as is_current,
    updated_at,
    measures
from scb

union all

select
    'kolada',
    kpi_id,
    title,
    coalesce(institution, 'Kolada (RKA)'),
    operating_area,
    operating_area,
    domain_id,
    'year',
    null,
    null,
    case municipality_type when 'L' then 'county' else 'municipality' end,
    scheduled_period is not null,
    null,
    null
from kolada

nodes.name: mart_symbol_atlas
nodes.subject: symbolic
nodes.description: One point per sampled symbol occurrence with its map position, cluster and context.

columns.name: occurrence_id
columns.description: Key: occurrence identifier, first 16 hex of the SHA-1 of document, character offset and symbol.

columns.name: symbol_id
columns.description: Foreign key to dim_symbol: the symbol whose word occurs.

columns.name: x
columns.description: Attribute: horizontal map coordinate from UMAP; unitless.

columns.name: y
columns.description: Attribute: vertical map coordinate from UMAP; unitless.

columns.name: cluster_id
columns.description: Attribute: HDBSCAN cluster number; -1 is noise. Numbered, never named.

columns.name: document_id
columns.description: Foreign key to dim_symbolic_document: the book the occurrence is in.

columns.name: title
columns.description: Attribute: title of the book.

columns.name: tradition
columns.description: Attribute: tradition of the book.

columns.name: matched_term
columns.description: Attribute: the word in the text that matched one of the symbol's aliases.

columns.name: context
columns.description: Attribute: previous sentence, matching sentence and next sentence, each cut to a window.

columns.name: cluster_probability
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: HDBSCAN membership probability for the cluster; 0-1.

columns.name: is_noise
columns.description: Attribute: true when cluster_id is -1.

nodes.sql:
-- One point on the Symbolic Atlas per sampled occurrence: where UMAP put its context, which
-- HDBSCAN cluster it fell in (numbered, never named; -1 is noise), and what it is.
select
    p.occurrence_id,
    o.symbol_id,
    o.document_id,
    d.title,
    o.tradition,
    o.matched_term,
    o.context,
    p.x,
    p.y,
    p.cluster_id,
    p.cluster_probability,
    p.is_noise
from {{ ref('stg_symbol_atlas_projection') }} as p
join {{ ref('int_symbol_occurrences') }} as o using (occurrence_id)
join {{ ref('int_symbolic_documents') }} as d using (document_id)

nodes.name: mart_symbol_profiles
nodes.subject: symbolic
nodes.description: Per symbol and cluster, how many occurrences and what share of the symbol's points.

columns.name: share_within_symbol
columns.description: Occurrences in this group / all occurrences of the symbol. Fraction from 0 to 1, not per cent.

columns.name: symbol_id
columns.description: Key, references dim_symbol: the symbol.

columns.name: occurrence_count
columns.description: Measure, additive: count of the symbol's sampled occurrences in the cluster.

columns.name: cluster_id
columns.description: Key: HDBSCAN cluster number; -1 is noise and is kept as a row.

columns.name: avg_cluster_probability
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: mean HDBSCAN membership probability of those occurrences; 0-1.

nodes.sql:
-- How each symbol's occurrences spread over the clusters: count, share of the symbol's points
-- and mean membership probability. Noise (-1) is a row like any cluster, so the shares add up.
select
    symbol_id,
    cluster_id,
    count(*) as occurrence_count,
    count(*) / sum(count(*)) over (partition by symbol_id) as share_within_symbol,
    avg(cluster_probability) as avg_cluster_probability
from {{ ref('mart_symbol_atlas') }}
group by symbol_id, cluster_id

nodes.name: mart_validity_history
nodes.subject: quality
nodes.description: Validity diagnostics across recorded runs, one row per analysis, run, experiment and metric.

columns.name: analysis_id
columns.description: Key: analysis id from the validity registry (currently symbolic_atlas_clustering's history).

columns.name: product_id
columns.description: Foreign key to dim_quality_product: the product the analysis belongs to.

columns.name: run_label
columns.description: Key: which recorded run: before_cleaning (before paratext cleaning) or current.

columns.name: experiment
columns.description: Key: the Symbolic Atlas experiment name, for example baseline.

columns.name: metric
columns.description: Key: metric name, for example mean_largest_book_share, mean_book_entropy, trustworthiness or silhouette.

columns.name: value
columns.description: Measure, non-additive: the metric's value in that run and experiment; unit set by the metric.

nodes.sql:
-- Validity diagnostics across recorded runs (for the Symbolic Atlas: before and after paratext
-- cleaning), so a change in a confounder's effect can be followed.
-- Cast, because an empty run writes untyped columns.
select
    cast(analysis_id as varchar) as analysis_id,
    cast(product_id as varchar) as product_id,
    cast(run_label as varchar) as run_label,
    cast(experiment as varchar) as experiment,
    cast(metric as varchar) as metric,
    cast(value as double) as value
from {{ ref('stg_quality_validity_history') }}

nodes.name: mart_vote_decisions
nodes.subject: politics
nodes.description: Roll calls in site order with their point and party positions; delivered per session.

columns.name: point_id
columns.description: Key: id of the committee report point the roll call decided.

columns.name: session
columns.description: Foreign key to dim_parliament_session: riksmöte of the decision point, e.g. 2024/25.

columns.name: slug
columns.description: Key: session folder name from the decision index path, e.g. 2024-25.

columns.name: file_order
columns.description: Key: 1-based position of the decision in the indexes, files in path order then rows in file order.

columns.name: decision
columns.description: Attribute: JSON decision object from the index, with point_id and the eight parties' positions and member vote counts added.

nodes.sql:
-- One row per roll call in site order: the index's decision with its committee point and the
-- eight parties' positions and member counts from fact_party_vote. Delivered as
-- gold/marts/votes/<session>.json.
with parties as (
    select vote_id, to_json(list({
        'party': party, 'party_position': party_position, 'yes_votes': yes_votes,
        'no_votes': no_votes, 'abstain_votes': abstain_votes, 'absent_votes': absent_votes
    } order by party)) as parties
    from {{ ref('stg_party_vote') }}
    group by vote_id
)
select
    d.slug,
    d.file_order,
    p.session,
    p.point_id,
    json_merge_patch(d.decision, json_object('point_id', p.point_id, 'parties', v.parties)) as decision
from {{ ref('stg_decision_index') }} as d
join {{ ref('stg_decision_point') }} as p on p.vote_id = d.vote_id
join parties as v on v.vote_id = d.vote_id

nodes.sql:
-- Documents matching each term per corpus, term list, language and month, summed over the counted
-- sources. A key term:lang is the pre-registered (primary) list, term:lang:amended the amended one.
select

    split_part(term_key, ':', 1) as term_id,

nodes.sql:
-- One row per stored file: when it was first and last fetched, from where and with which hash.
-- A file is one published text (acts/), or one version of a page or query answer (@<sha12>).
select
    path,
    any_value(url) as url,
    any_value(sha256) as sha256,
    min(cast(fetched_at as timestamptz)) as first_fetched_at,
    max(cast(fetched_at as timestamptz)) as last_fetched_at,
    count(*) as fetch_count,
    any_value(logical_path) as logical_path
from {{ source('eu_ai_act', 'fetches') }}
where method = 'GET'
group by path

nodes.name: stg_ai_act_guidance_pages
nodes.subject: ai_act
nodes.description: Every stored version of each Commission guidance page.
nodes.sql:
-- Every stored version of each Commission guidance page, with the page's entry in the list.
with files as (
    select
        regexp_extract(replace(filename, '\', '/'), 'guidance/(.+)@[0-9a-f]+\.html$', 1) as guidance_id,
        'guidance/' || regexp_extract(replace(filename, '\', '/'), 'guidance/(.+\.html)$', 1) as path,
        content as html
    from {{ source('eu_ai_act', 'guidance_pages') }}
)

select
    files.guidance_id,
    s.kind,
    s.url as source_url,
    to_json(s.articles) as articles_json,
    files.path,
    f.sha256 as source_hash,
    f.first_fetched_at,
    f.last_fetched_at,
    files.html
from files
join {{ source('eu_ai_act', 'guidance_sources') }} as s
    on s.id = files.guidance_id
left join {{ ref('stg_ai_act_fetches') }} as f
    on f.path = files.path

nodes.name: stg_ai_act_related
nodes.subject: ai_act
nodes.description: Every distinct Cellar answer on related documents; is_latest marks the one silver reads.
nodes.sql:
-- Every distinct Cellar answer, newest first per query: `related` (documents pointing to the
-- act) and `origin` (the proposal the act adopts). Silver reads the latest of each; older answers
-- stay so the history of what Cellar listed is kept.
with files as (
    select
        'cellar/' || regexp_extract(replace(filename, '\', '/'), 'cellar/((related|origin)@[0-9a-f]+\.json)$', 1) as path,
        regexp_extract(replace(filename, '\', '/'), 'cellar/(related|origin)@', 1) as query,
        content
    from {{ source('eu_ai_act', 'related') }}
)

select
    files.path,
    files.query,
    f.sha256 as source_hash,
    f.url as source_url,
    f.first_fetched_at,
    f.last_fetched_at,
    files.content as answer_json,
    row_number() over (partition by files.query order by f.last_fetched_at desc, f.first_fetched_at desc) = 1 as is_latest
from files
left join {{ ref('stg_ai_act_fetches') }} as f
    on f.path = files.path

nodes.name: stg_ai_act_texts
nodes.subject: ai_act
nodes.description: One row per act text (CELEX number × language) as served by the Publications Office.

columns.name: source_hash
columns.description: SHA-256 of the bytes Cellar served (warehouse/raw/eu_ai_act/_manifest.jsonl).

nodes.sql:
-- One row per act text as served by Cellar: CELEX number, language, the XHTML and its provenance.
with files as (
    select
        replace(filename, '\', '/') as filename,
        content
    from {{ source('eu_ai_act', 'texts') }}
),

named as (
    select
        regexp_extract(filename, 'acts/(.+)\.([a-z]{2})\.xhtml$', 1) as celex,
        regexp_extract(filename, 'acts/(.+)\.([a-z]{2})\.xhtml$', 2) as language,
        'acts/' || regexp_extract(filename, 'acts/(.+\.xhtml)$', 1) as path,
        content as xhtml
    from files
)

select
    n.celex,
    n.language,
    n.path,
    f.url as source_url,
    f.sha256 as source_hash,
    f.first_fetched_at as retrieved_at,
    f.last_fetched_at as last_checked_at,
    n.xhtml
from named as n
left join {{ ref('stg_ai_act_fetches') }} as f
    on f.path = n.path

nodes.sql:
-- Nationella folkhälsoenkäten, all six tables stacked. One row per table, measure, region
-- or age group, sex and period. The statistic variable splits each value into share,
-- interval bounds and number of responses; silver pivots them.
{% set tables = {
    'hlv1psyxreg': ('Psykisk hälsa', 'region'), 'hlv1psyaald': ('Psykisk hälsa', 'age'),
    'hlv1allmxreg': ('Hälsotillstånd', 'region'), 'hlv1allmaald': ('Hälsotillstånd', 'age'),
    'hlv1socxreg': ('Sociala relationer', 'region'), 'hlv1socaald': ('Sociala relationer', 'age'),
} %}
{% for table, (measure_variable, breakdown) in tables.items() %}
select
    '{{ table }}' as source_table,
    '{{ breakdown }}' as breakdown,
    {{ px_dim(measure_variable) }} as measure_code,
    {% if breakdown == 'region' %}{{ px_dim('Region') }}{% else %}null{% endif %} as region_code,
    {% if breakdown == 'age' %}{{ px_dim('Ålder') }}{% else %}null{% endif %} as age_code,
    {{ px_dim('Kön') }} as sex_code,
    {{ px_dim('År') }} as period_code,
    {{ px_dim('Andel och konfidensintervall') }} as statistic_code,
    {{ px_value(1) }} as value,
    {{ px_marker(1) }} as value_marker,
    filename as source_file
from ({{ pxweb_rows(source('fohm', table)) }})
{% if not loop.last %}union all{% endif %}
{% endfor %}

nodes.name: stg_job_ads
nodes.subject: jobs
nodes.description: Latest observed payload per source job ID. Strings are trimmed and dates safely cast; timestamps retain source wall time.

columns.name: job_id
columns.description: Canonical ad ID; historical-original plus original_id when available, otherwise source record ID. The archive record ID is retained separately.

columns.name: published_at
columns.description: Source publication timestamp. A failed cast fails the not-null test for review.

columns.name: required_skills
columns.description: Source must-have skill objects, retained as JSON; keyword mentions are derived separately.

nodes.sql:
-- A table, not a view: four gold models read it, and re-parsing the payload JSON in each
-- of them spilled gigabytes of temporary files on a full archive build.
{{ config(materialized="table") }}

with identified as (
    select * exclude (job_id), job_id as source_record_id,
        case when source_kind = 'historical' and nullif(trim(payload ->> '$.original_id'), '') is not null
            then 'historical-original:' || trim(payload ->> '$.original_id')
            else job_id end as job_id
    from {{ source('jobtech', 'job_ads') }}
), latest as (
    select * from identified
    qualify row_number() over (partition by job_id order by ingestion_id desc) = 1
), cleaned as (
    select
        job_id, source_record_id,
        {{ clean_string("payload ->> '$.headline'") }} as title,
        {{ clean_string("payload ->> '$.employer.organization_number'") }} as organization_number,
        {{ clean_string("payload ->> '$.employer.name'") }} as employer_name,
        {{ clean_string("payload ->> '$.workplace_address.municipality_code'") }} as municipality_code,
        {{ clean_string("payload ->> '$.workplace_address.municipality'") }} as municipality,
        {{ clean_string("payload ->> '$.workplace_address.region'") }} as region,
        {{ clean_string("payload ->> '$.workplace_address.country'") }} as country,
        {{ clean_string(taxonomy_value('occupation', 'concept_id')) }} as occupation_code,
        {{ clean_string(taxonomy_value('occupation', 'label')) }} as occupation,
        {{ clean_string(taxonomy_value('occupation_field', 'concept_id')) }} as occupation_field_id,
        {{ clean_string("payload ->> '$.original_id'") }} as original_id,
        try_cast(payload ->> '$.number_of_vacancies' as integer) as number_of_vacancies,
        try_cast(payload ->> '$.publication_date' as timestamp) as published_at,
        try_cast(payload ->> '$.application_deadline' as timestamp) as last_application_date,
        {{ clean_string(taxonomy_value('employment_type', 'label')) }} as employment_type,
        coalesce(payload ->> '$.description.text', '') as description,
        coalesce(json_extract(payload, '$.must_have.skills'), '[]'::json) as required_skills,
        ingestion_id, ingested_at, source_kind
    from latest
)
select *,
    md5(coalesce('org:' || organization_number, 'name:' || lower(employer_name), 'unknown')) as employer_id,
    md5(to_json(list_value(country, municipality_code, municipality, region))) as location_id,
    md5(coalesce('code:' || occupation_code, 'label:' || lower(occupation), 'unknown')) as occupation_id
from cleaned

columns.name: match_class

nodes.sql:
-- One row per matched ad, unpacked from rank.py's match store. No approved profile means no rows.
with store as (
    select json from {{ source('job_assistant', 'matches') }}
),
rows as (
    select unnest(from_json(json -> 'matches', '["JSON"]')) as m from store
)
select
    m ->> 'id' as ad_id,
    cast(m ->> 'rank' as integer) as rank,
    m ->> 'class' as match_class,
    m ->> 'role' as role,
    cast(m ->> 'role_from_title' as boolean) as role_from_title,
    from_json(m -> 'reasons', '["VARCHAR"]') as reasons,
    coalesce(from_json(m -> 'gaps', '["VARCHAR"]'), []) as gaps,
    coalesce(from_json(m -> 'uncertain', '["VARCHAR"]'), []) as uncertain,
    try_cast(m ->> 'similarity' as double) as similarity,
    m ->> 'remote' as remote_quote,
    m -> 'seniority' ->> 'title' as senior_title,
    try_cast(m -> 'seniority' ->> 'years' as integer) as years_asked,
    m -> 'seniority' ->> 'junior' as junior_quote,
    m -> 'explanation' ->> 'status' as explanation_status,
    m -> 'explanation' ->> 'text' as explanation,
    m -> 'explanation' ->> 'model' as explanation_model,
    m ->> 'content_hash' as content_hash,
    cast(m ->> 'profile_version' as integer) as profile_version,
    m ->> 'cv_sha256' as cv_sha256,
    m ->> 'engine' as engine,
    m -> 'skills' as skills,
    m -> 'checks' as checks
from rows

nodes.sql:
-- Ads per month and occupation field, summed over archives (an archive covers a year or a
-- quarter; a month can straddle two when ads are republished, so counts are summed).
select
    cast(publication_month || '-01' as date) as month,
    field_id,
    any_value(field) as field,
    sum(ads) as ads
from {{ source('jobtech_governance', 'totals') }}
-- A few ads carry impossible publication dates (2051, 2099); months after the build date are left out.
where publication_month >= '2020-01' and publication_month <= strftime(current_date, '%Y-%m')
group by 1, 2

nodes.name: stg_kb_libraries
nodes.subject: sweden
nodes.sql:
-- One row per library in Biblioteksdatabasen, in the dump's order (file, then position). Only
-- what SWEDEN D uses; no contact details.
with files as (
    select filename, unnest(json_extract(content, '$.libraries[*]')) as l,
           generate_subscripts(json_extract(content, '$.libraries[*]'), 1) as position
    from {{ source('kb', 'libraries') }}
)
select
    l ->> 'sigel' as sigel,
    l ->> 'name' as name,
    l ->> 'municipality_code' as municipality_code,
    l ->> 'library_type' as library_type,
    cast(l ->> 'alive' as boolean) as alive,
    l ->> 'country_code' as country_code,
    cast(l ->> 'longitude' as double) as longitude,
    cast(l ->> 'latitude' as double) as latitude,
    row_number() over (order by filename, position) as dump_order
from files

nodes.name: stg_kb_statistics
nodes.subject: sweden
nodes.sql:
-- One row per bibstat observation: term, library (sigel), year, target group and value. A value
-- that is absent or not a number stays NULL here; gold decides what that means.
with files as (
    select
        regexp_extract(filename, '([A-Za-z0-9]+)\.json$', 1) as term,
        unnest(json_extract(content, '$.observations[*]')) as o
    from {{ source('kb', 'statistics') }}
)
select
    o ->> '$."@id"' as observation_id,
    term,
    regexp_extract(o ->> '$.library."@id"', '[^/]+$') as sigel,
    cast(o ->> 'sampleYear' as integer) as sample_year,
    o ->> 'targetGroup' as target_group,
    case when json_type(o -> term) in ('BIGINT', 'UBIGINT', 'DOUBLE')
        then cast(o ->> term as double) end as value
from files

nodes.name: stg_market_ads
nodes.subject: market
nodes.sql:
-- Ads and vacancies per month, occupation group and county, from every archive since 2020.
-- A few ads carry a publication date outside their archive's period (a handful in the year
-- before, some far in the future); only months from 2020 up to the current month count.
-- The county is the ad's workplace county; ads with none, or "Ospecificerad arbetsort",
-- are kept as an unknown county so national totals stay whole.
-- Each archive counts only its own period (its year, or its quarter), so an ad that appears
-- in two archives (republished across the turn of a year) is counted once. The daily stream
-- (ingest_stream.py, archive 'stream') counts only the months after the archives end; those
-- months are preliminary and are replaced when their archive is published.
with source as (
    select
        cast(publication_month || '-01' as date) as month,
        field_id,
        field,
        group_id,
        ssyk,
        occupation_group,
        case
            when region is null or region in ('', 'Ospecificerad arbetsort') then 'Okänt län'
            else region
        end as region,
        ads,
        vacancies,
        regexp_extract(filename, '_(\d{4}(-Q\d)?|stream)\.parquet$', 1) as archive
    from {{ source('jobtech_market', 'ads') }}
    where publication_month similar to '\d{4}-\d{2}'
),
-- The last day the archives cover: a year archive ends on 31 December, a quarter's on the
-- quarter's last day.
archives_end as (
    select max(case when archive like '%-Q%'
                    then last_day(make_date(cast(left(archive, 4) as integer),
                                            cast(right(archive, 1) as integer) * 3, 1))
                    else make_date(cast(archive as integer), 12, 31) end) as last_day
    from source
    where archive <> 'stream'
)
select
    month, field_id, field, group_id, ssyk, occupation_group, region, archive,
    sum(ads)::bigint as ads,
    sum(vacancies)::bigint as vacancies
from source
where month between date '2020-01-01' and date_trunc('month', current_date)
  and (
        case when archive = 'stream'
            then month > (select last_day from archives_end)
            when archive like '%-Q%'
            then year(month) = cast(left(archive, 4) as integer)
             and quarter(month) = cast(right(archive, 1) as integer)
            else year(month) = cast(archive as integer)
        end)
group by all

nodes.name: stg_market_conditions
nodes.subject: market
nodes.sql:
-- Ads per month and occupation field by conditions of employment. The 2020-2021 archives
-- write employment type and working hours as upper-case codes (VANLIG_ANSTALLNING, HELTID);
-- later archives write labels (Vanlig anställning, Heltid). Both map to the later labels.
-- Each archive counts only its own period (its year, or its quarter), so an ad that appears
-- in two archives (republished across the turn of a year) is counted once. The daily stream
-- (ingest_stream.py, archive 'stream') counts only the months after the archives end; those
-- months are preliminary and are replaced when their archive is published.
with source as (
    select
        cast(publication_month || '-01' as date) as month,
        field_id,
        case upper(replace(coalesce(employment_type, ''), ' ', '_'))
            when 'VANLIG_ANSTÄLLNING' then 'Vanlig anställning'
            when 'VANLIG_ANSTALLNING' then 'Vanlig anställning'
            when 'BEHOVSANSTÄLLNING' then 'Behovsanställning'
            when 'BEHOVSANSTALLNING' then 'Behovsanställning'
            when 'SOMMARJOBB' then 'Sommarjobb / feriejobb'
            when 'SOMMARJOBB_/_FERIEJOBB' then 'Sommarjobb / feriejobb'
            when 'ARBETE_UTOMLANDS' then 'Arbete utomlands'
            when 'FERIEJOBB' then 'Sommarjobb / feriejobb'
            when '' then 'Okänd'
            else employment_type
        end as employment_type,
        -- Part of the 2024 archive gives the duration here ("Tillsvidare", "6 månader eller
        -- längre") instead of the working hours; those count as not stated.
        case upper(coalesce(working_hours, ''))
            when 'HELTID' then 'Heltid'
            when 'DELTID' then 'Deltid'
            else 'Okänd'
        end as working_hours,
        experience_required,
        ads,
        vacancies,
        regexp_extract(filename, '_(\d{4}(-Q\d)?|stream)\.parquet$', 1) as archive
    from {{ source('jobtech_market', 'conditions') }}
    where publication_month similar to '\d{4}-\d{2}'
),
-- The last day the archives cover: a year archive ends on 31 December, a quarter's on the
-- quarter's last day.
archives_end as (
    select max(case when archive like '%-Q%'
                    then last_day(make_date(cast(left(archive, 4) as integer),
                                            cast(right(archive, 1) as integer) * 3, 1))
                    else make_date(cast(archive as integer), 12, 31) end) as last_day
    from source
    where archive <> 'stream'
)
select
    month, field_id, employment_type, working_hours, experience_required,
    sum(ads)::bigint as ads,
    sum(vacancies)::bigint as vacancies
from source
where month >= date '2020-01-01'
  and month <= (select max(month) from {{ ref('stg_market_ads') }})
  and (
        case when archive = 'stream'
            then month > (select last_day from archives_end)
            when archive like '%-Q%'
            then year(month) = cast(left(archive, 4) as integer)
             and quarter(month) = cast(right(archive, 1) as integer)
            else year(month) = cast(archive as integer)
        end)
group by all
